# Dynamic context discovery

![](/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Favatars%2Fjediah-katz.jpeg&w=48&q=70)

Jediah Katz · 6 min read

### Table of Contents

↑

-   [Files for dynamic context discovery](#files-for-dynamic-context-discovery)
-   [1\. Turning long tool responses into files](#1-turning-long-tool-responses-into-files)
-   [2\. Referencing chat history during summarization](#2-referencing-chat-history-during-summarization)
-   [3\. Supporting the Agent Skills open standard](#3-supporting-the-agent-skills-open-standard)
-   [4\. Efficiently loading only the MCP tools needed](#4-efficiently-loading-only-the-mcp-tools-needed)
-   [5\. Treating all integrated terminal sessions as files](#5-treating-all-integrated-terminal-sessions-as-files)
-   [Simple abstractions](#simple-abstractions)

Coding agents are quickly changing how software is built. Their rapid improvement comes from both improved agentic models and better context engineering to steer them.

Cursor's agent harness, the instructions and tools we provide the model, is optimized individually for every new frontier model we support. However, there are context engineering improvements we can make, such as how we gather context and optimize token usage over a long trajectory, that apply to all models inside our harness.

As models have become better as agents, we've found success by providing fewer details up front, making it easier for the agent to pull relevant context on its own. We're calling this pattern **dynamic context discovery**, in contrast to *static context* which is always included.

## [#](#files-for-dynamic-context-discovery)Files for dynamic context discovery

Dynamic context discovery is far more token-efficient, as only the necessary data is pulled into the context window. It can also improve the agent's response quality by reducing the amount of potentially confusing or contradictory information in the context window.

Here's how we've used dynamic context discovery in Cursor:

1.  Turning long tool responses into files
2.  Referencing chat history during summarization
3.  Supporting the Agent Skills open standard
4.  Efficiently loading only the MCP tools needed
5.  Treating all integrated terminal sessions as files

## [#](#1-turning-long-tool-responses-into-files)1\. Turning long tool responses into files

Tool calls can dramatically increase the context window by returning a large JSON response.

For first-party tools in Cursor, like editing files and searching the codebase, we can prevent context bloat with intelligent tool definitions and minimal response formats, but third-party tools (i.e. shell commands or MCP calls) don't natively get this same treatment.

The common approach coding agents take is to truncate long shell commands or MCP results. This can lead to data loss, which could include important information you wanted in the context. In Cursor, we instead write the output to a file and give the agent the ability to read it. The agent calls `tail` to check the end, and then read more if it needs to.

This has resulted in fewer unnecessary summarizations when reaching context limits.

## [#](#2-referencing-chat-history-during-summarization)2\. Referencing chat history during summarization

When the model's context window fills up, Cursor triggers a summarization step to give the agent a fresh context window with a summary of its work so far.

But the agent's knowledge can degrade after summarization since it's a lossy compression of the context. The agent might have forgotten crucial details about its task. In Cursor, we use the chat history as files to improve the quality of summarization.

![](/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fpast-chats-light.png&w=3840&q=70)![](/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fpast-chats-dark.png&w=3840&q=70)

After the context window limit is reached, or the user decides to summarize manually, we give the agent a reference to the history file. If the agent knows that it needs more details that are missing from the summary, it can search through the history to recover them.

## [#](#3-supporting-the-agent-skills-open-standard)3\. Supporting the Agent Skills open standard

Cursor supports [Agent Skills](https://cursor.com/docs/skills), an open standard for extending coding agents with specialized capabilities. Similar to other types of [Rules](https://cursor.com/docs/rules), Skills are defined by files that tell the agent how to perform on a domain-specific task.

Skills also include a name and description which can be included as "static context" in the system prompt. The agent can then do dynamic context discovery to pull in relevant skills, using tools like grep and Cursor's [semantic search](https://cursor.com/blog/semsearch).

Skills can also bundle executables or scripts relevant to the task. Since they're just files, the agent can easily find what's relevant to a particular skill.

## [#](#4-efficiently-loading-only-the-mcp-tools-needed)4\. Efficiently loading only the MCP tools needed

MCP is helpful for accessing secured resources behind OAuth. That could be production logs, external design files, or internal context and documentation for an enterprise.

Some MCP servers include many tools, often with long descriptions, which can significantly bloat the context window. Most of these tools go unused even though they are always included in the prompt. This compounds if you use multiple MCP servers.

It's not feasible to expect every MCP server to optimize for this. We believe it's the responsibility of the coding agents to reduce context usage. In Cursor, we support dynamic context discovery for MCP by syncing tool descriptions to a folder.[1](#fn-1)

The agent now only receives a small bit of static context, including names of the tools, prompting it to look up tools when the task calls for it. In an A/B test, we found that in runs that called an MCP tool, this strategy **reduced total agent tokens by 46.9%** (statistically significant, with high variance based on the number of MCPs installed).

![](/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fmcp-tools-light-3.png&w=3840&q=70)![](/marketing-static/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fptht05hbb1ssoooe.public.blob.vercel-storage.com%2Fassets%2Fblog%2Fmcp-tools-dark-3.png&w=3840&q=70)

This file approach also unlocks the ability to communicate the status of MCP tools to the agent. For example, previously if an MCP server needed re-authentication, the agent would forget about those tools entirely, leaving the user confused. Now, it can actually let the user know to re-authenticate proactively.

## [#](#5-treating-all-integrated-terminal-sessions-as-files)5\. Treating all integrated terminal sessions as files

Rather than needing to copy/paste the output of a terminal session into the agent input, Cursor now syncs the integrated terminal outputs to the local filesystem.

This makes it easy to ask "why did my command fail?" and allow the agent to understand what you're referencing. Since terminal history can be long, the agent can grep for only the relevant outputs, which is useful for logs from a long-running process like a server.

This mirrors what CLI-based coding agents see, with prior shell output in context, but discovered dynamically rather than injected statically.

## [#](#simple-abstractions)Simple abstractions

It's not clear if files will be the final interface for LLM-based tools.

But as coding agents quickly improve, files have been a simple and powerful primitive to use, and a safer choice than yet another abstraction that can't fully account for the future. Stay tuned for lots more exciting work to share in this space.

These improvements will be live for all users in the coming weeks. The techniques described in this blog post are the work of many Cursor employees including Lukas Moller, Yash Gaitonde, Wilson Lin, Jason Ma, Devang Jhabakh, and Jediah Katz. If you are interested in solving the hardest and most ambitious coding tasks using AI, we'd love to hear from you. Reach out to us at [hiring@cursor.com](mailto:hiring@cursor.com).

---

1.  We considered a tool search approach, but that would scatter tools across a flat index. Instead, we create one folder per server, keeping each server's tools logically grouped. When the model lists a folder, it sees all tools from that server together and can understand them as a cohesive unit. Files also enable more powerful searching. The agent can use full `rg` parameters or even `jq` to filter tool descriptions. [↩](#fnref-1)

# PRAANA per-turn context compilation — research report

## Executive summary (key architectural facts for your evaluation)

1. **The provider `messages[]` array never accumulates cross-turn history.** Each `runTurn()` builds a fresh `history` containing only the current user input plus that turn's tool-loop steps. All cross-turn context lives in a **single compiled system prompt string** regenerated from scratch every turn. An "append-only messages + compaction" design would be a genuine architectural change.
2. **Two compilers exist**: classic (full verbatim history, no truncation, plus an existing LLM-based auto-compaction at 75% fill) and engine (a large scored/budgeted/density-weighted pipeline with checkpoints, artifacts, workflow context, BM25+semantic ranking).
3. **Compaction already exists** — but only for classic mode (`src/auto-compact.ts`): oldest 25% of events → LLM-summarized into Cognitive Memory facts → events marked "compressed" and excluded from prompt assembly. Engine mode instead degrades rendering via pressure modes (no history rewrite).
4. **Full history is already durably stored and searchable**: `events.jsonl` (append-only, fsync'd, complete tool results) plus a SQLite turn ledger with BM25 search. `search_session_log` / `search_turn_events` already implement the "searchable history" half of your proposed design.
5. Note: AGENTS.md mentions "pi-ai", but the codebase has **replaced pi-ai with a native LLM subsystem** (`src/llm/`, "zero external provider SDK dependencies"); there is no pi-ai dependency in `package.json`.

---

## 1. `src/turn.ts` (1752 lines) — per-turn orchestration

### Mode selection — `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:467-470`
```ts
const contextEngineEnabled = session.isContextEngineEnabled?.() ?? session.config.context_engine?.enabled ?? false;
const useEngineCompiler = contextEngineEnabled && !!session.contextEngine;
const classicMode = !useEngineCompiler;
```
Engine mode requires config enabled (default `true`, `src/config.ts:149`) **and** a successfully initialized `session.contextEngine` (opened in `src/session.ts:1640`; failures fall back to classic, `src/session.ts:1660-1666`).

### Per-turn sequence in `runTurn()` (`src/turn.ts:429-1470`)

| Step | Lines | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Snapshot | 448-451 | `TurnRecorder` created; `captureStateSnapshot(stateGraph)` for later diff |
| Log input | 454-458 | `user_message` event appended to event log |
| Plan approval | 462-464 | `/plan` approval-word detection |
| Auto-hydrate (engine only) | 476-499 | `stateGraph.autoHydrate(userInput)` promotes matching peripheral objects; logs `context_action setTier reason=auto_hydrate` |
| Build tools | 504-562 | `createAllTools(...)` with scorecard/artifact/lsp wiring; `classicMode` flag gates engine-only tools |
| Context window | 565-566 | `session.ensureModelContextWindow(modelName)` (async catalog lookup); `reserved_output_tokens` read |
| Recent events | 569-571 | `readLastUncompressedAfterResetBoundary(config.compiler.recent_turns)` (default 10) — passed in `compileInput` but **ignored by the engine compiler** (it uses ledger `turnRecords` instead) |
| Compile inputs | 574-606 | skills catalog (`buildSkillMetadataCatalog`), engine config, checkpoint (`getVisibleSessionCheckpoint`, reset-boundary aware), resume note, budgets |
| pre_compile hooks | 608-611 | `session.hooks.runPreCompile(...)` |
| **Engine compile** | 616-681 | `EmbeddingCache` lazily created; workflow patterns + file-read index fetched; `compileEngineWithMetrics(...)`; stores score records, pressure mode, compile telemetry; debug writes `scores.jsonl` |
| **Classic compile** | 682-730 | `compileClassicWithMetrics(...)`; then **`maybeAutoCompactClassic()`** (700-704); if compacted, re-runs compilation with the now-filtered events (710-727) |
| Provider/model | 754-785 | `createProvider(effectiveLlm, contextWindowTokens)(resolveModel(modelName))` + OAuth overlay |
| Stream loop | 803-1337 | `history = [{role:"user", content:userInput}]` (803-809); up to `turn.max_steps` (default 25, line 810); `attemptStream()` → `runLlmStream()`; step-0 retry + fallback provider (938-957) |
| Tool execution | 1067-1305 | log `tool_call` (args secret-redacted for the log only, 1068); pre hooks → concurrent `Promise.all` execute → post hooks (1113-1137); engine mode ingests results via `contextEngine.ingestToolResult()` and may replace prompt text with an artifact card (1208-1267); results pushed to `history` (1285-1292) and `tool_result` events appended with the **full raw result** (1294-1298) |

| Memory banner | 1454-1467 | stats + scorecard nudge |

### Tier management — `applyTierManagement()` `src/turn.ts:1580-1604`
Demotes active objects by idle turns (`config.tiers.idle_soft_after_turns=20`, `idle_hard_after_turns=50`, `src/config.ts:79-82`). Interrupted turns go through `finalizeInterruptedTurn()` (`src/turn.ts:1472-1542`) which mirrors the same finalization.

### LLM stream wrapper — `runLlmStream()` `src/turn.ts:121-304`
Normalizes the loose `history` entries into canonical `ConversationMessage[]` (user / assistant / tool_result / system, lines 122-173), maps tool defs (175-179), and calls `streamLlmResponse({ systemPrompt: compiledPrompt, messages, tools, ... })` (196-212). Collects text deltas, tool calls, usage, final message.

## 2. `src/compile-classic.ts` (209 lines) — classic compiler

**Exports:** `buildClassicSystemFrame` (28), `excludeCurrentUserInputFromEvents` (89), `buildFullConversationHistory` (104), `compileClassicWithMetrics` (149).

**Prompt assembly** (`compileClassicWithMetrics`, lines 149-209), sections joined by `\n\n`:
1. **System frame** (28-86): identity/version, cwd, session id, timestamp, `## Project Context` (merged AGENTS.md), `## Project Stack`, resume note, native-addon status, shared agent policy (`buildSharedAgentPolicy` from compiler.ts), skills/memory usage blurb.
2. **Circuit notes** (165-166) if any.
3. **Skills catalog** (168-172) — verbatim, no trim in classic.
4. **Cross-session memory digest** (174-178) via `buildCrossSessionMemory` — verbatim, no trim.
5. **Full conversation history** (180-183) via `buildFullConversationHistory` (104-147): every event after the last `reset_boundary` except `context_action`/`system_note`/`ui_transcript`, rendered as `User: …` / `PRAANA: …` / `Tool call: name({args})` / `Result (name): {full JSON}`.

**Size/limits:** **There is no truncation or budgeting in classic mode.** Tool results are rendered as full `JSON.stringify(result)`. The prompt grows unboundedly with the session; metrics always report `recentTurnsTruncated: false` (lines 203-206). The only backstop is:
- **Auto-compaction** (`maybeAutoCompactClassic`, invoked from turn.ts:700) which removes oldest events from the log view once prompt tokens exceed 75% of the usable window (see §7).
- The current user input is **not** duplicated in the prompt; it goes via `messages[]` (comment at line 185).

## 3. `src/compiler.ts` (751 lines) + `src/context-engine/engine-compiler.ts` (955 lines)

### `src/compiler.ts` — legacy budget-band compiler + shared section builders
Per AGENTS.md the budget-band `compile()`/`compileWithMetrics()` (lines 69-240) are **unit-test-only legacy**; runtime uses the two `*WithMetrics` compilers. But this file supplies the shared builders both modes use:

- `buildSharedAgentPolicy()` (244-282) — mode-neutral policy text.
- `buildArtifactFirstReadsPolicy()` (284-290), `buildAgentHints()` (306-322), `REPEAT_FILE_READS_THRESHOLD = 5` (302).
- `buildFilesReadIndexSection()` (335-363) — "Files Read This Session" path→artifact index (cap 25 entries).
- `buildSystemFrame()` (365-446) — engine system frame incl. Implicit Knowledge Capture + Memory Management instructions.
- `buildCrossSessionMemory()` (448-456), `buildActiveState()` (458-477), `buildPeripheralStubs()` (479-496), `calculateTokenSavings()` (503-538).
- Legacy recent-turns renderer with truncation (540-613): assistant text capped 800 chars; tool results 500 chars (200 for read/write_file); token-budget cutoff marker.
- `trimSectionToTokenBudget()` (709-731), `trimAgentsContext()` (733-751) — line-based trimming used by both runtime compilers.
- `CompileMetrics` interface (35-64) — per-section token metrics + truncation flags.

### `src/context-engine/engine-compiler.ts` — the engine compiler
**Constants (lines 54-56):** `BAND_VERBATIM_TOKENS = 3000`, `BAND_SCORED_RECENT_TOKENS = 3000`, `BAND_SCORED_OLDER_TOKENS = 2000`.

Key functions:
- `renderVerbatimTurn` (124-139), `renderTurnDigest` (141-158), `buildArtifactUnit` (160-193), `buildScoredUnits` (195-262).
- `buildVerbatimSection` (264-308): last ≤2 turns, progressive trim (drop oldest first; single-turn tail-keep char truncation).
- `resolvePressureMode` (309-316) vs `pressure.compact_at=0.7` / `emergency_at=0.85`; `resolveRawSafetyMode` (333-342) escalates on raw-token overflow.
- `computeWeightedTokens` (397-418) — density-weighted total (see §8).
- `compileEnginePass` (467-698) — one full prompt build. **Section order:** system frame → skills (ratio-trimmed) → agent hints → circuit notes → workflow context → checkpoint (pressure-mode-aware) → files-read index → verbatim turns → **Scored Context** → cross-session memory (ratio-trimmed) → active state → peripheral stubs.
  - Scored units: turns age 3-6 become `turn_digest` units + artifact cards; age >6 only artifact cards (dropped entirely in `compact` mode; `emergency` keeps only current-turn artifact cards). Activity entries become units too.
  - Scoring: `precomputeVectors` (embedder, cache) → `rankContextUnits` for a recent band (age 3-6) and older band (age >6) → `selectUnitsWithinBudget` per band (lines 562-653).
- `compileEngineWithMetrics` (737-921) — the orchestrator:
  1. `classifyTask` via domain classifier (740-746).
  2. **Task-type-aware band scaling** (748-778): scales the three band caps + checkpoint section budgets by budget-allocation ratios (clamped, min caps 50/200 tokens).
  3. Preliminary weighted estimate → checkpoint pressure mode (796-822).
  4. Pass 1 → weighted tokens → pressure mode; re-run pass if escalated (834-853).
  5. Raw safety mode check; possible third pass (855-893).
  6. Returns `EngineCompileResult`: prompt, metrics, per-unit `scoreRecords`, `pressureRatio` (weighted), `rawPressureRatio`, `excludedScoredUnits`, `taskType`, `budgetAllocation`.
- `explainUnitScore` (923-953) backs the `/why` command.

**Complexity assessment:** engine-compiler alone is ~955 lines; with scoring (105), density (65), checkpoint (753), extraction (144), turn-digest (325), artifact-store (587), telemetry (714), db (1116), workflow-tracker (292) the engine subsystem is **~6,000+ lines** supporting the per-turn compile, versus ~210 lines for classic.

## 5. `src/state-graph.ts` (356) + `src/state-graph-checkpoint.ts` (125)

### StateGraph (`src/state-graph.ts`)
- In-memory `Map<id, StateObject>` + `touchedTurn` map (21-23). Kinds: task/decision/constraint/note; tiers: active/soft/hard.
- `create` (31), `update` (47), `setTier` (57), `retractObject` (66), `getActive` (81, focused-first), `getPeripheral` (105), `setFocus` (93), `list` (112), `snapshot` (125).
- **`autoHydrate(query)`** (178-211): two passes over peripheral objects — (1) substring keyword match (stop-word-filtered keywords ≥3 chars), (2) BM25 relevance ≥ `BM25_HYDRATE_THRESHOLD = 0.15`. Returns `{id, text, method}[]`; texts feed the scoring `hydrate_boost`.
- `replayAction` (214-273): rebuilds state from `context_action` event payloads (create/update/setTier/setFocus/retract) — used on resume when no checkpoint exists.
- `exportCheckpoint` / `restoreFromCheckpoint` (142-171).

### O(1) resume (`src/state-graph-checkpoint.ts`)
- `StateGraphCheckpoint` JSON (15-32): objects + touched_turn + both turn counters + `last_event_id`.
- `saveStateGraphCheckpoint` (68-85): write tmp + `fsyncSync` + rename (crash-safe), to `state_graph_checkpoint.json` in the session dir.
- `loadStateGraphCheckpoint` (43-66) with validation; `findReplayStartIndex` (95-102); `replayStateGraphFromEvents` (104-125): resume = restore snapshot, then replay only `context_action` events **after** `last_event_id` (plus `state_reset` notes). Persisted every turn by `session.persistStateGraphCheckpoint()` (`src/session.ts:689-700`, called at turn.ts:1450).

## 6. Event log storage + `search_session_log`

### `src/event-log.ts` (482)
- `EventLog.append` (150-185): assigns ULID, `writeSync` + **`fsyncSync`** per event, maintains an in-memory parse cache invalidated by mtime/size (105-137).
- **Storage fidelity:** `tool_call` payloads store args (secret-redacted copy), `tool_result` payloads store the **complete result object** (turn.ts:1294-1298); `agent_message` stores full assistant text; `user_message` full text. Nothing is truncated at log time.
- Read APIs: `readAll` (191), `readLast` (187), `readAllUncompressed` (203), `readAllAfterResetBoundary` (210), `readAllUncompressedAfterResetBoundary` (215), `readLastUncompressedAfterResetBoundary` (222), `replayContextActions` (226).
- **`search(query, options)`** (238-266): case-insensitive substring; whitespace = AND, `|` = OR; optional `kinds` filter; `afterResetBoundary` option; default limit 20; 400-char excerpts. `eventSearchText` (371-390) covers user/agent text, tool name + JSON args, tool name + JSON result, ui_transcript, context_action, system_note.
- Compaction support: `markEventsAsCompressed(ids)` (294-300) persists a `compression_checkpoint.json` set; compressed events are excluded from `readAllUncompressed*` but **remain in the file and in `search()`** (search reads `internalRead()`, not the uncompressed view) — so compaction is a prompt-assembly filter, never a deletion.
- Reset boundaries: `logResetBoundary` (281), `eventsAfterResetBoundary` (351), `findLastResetBoundaryTurn` (361) — the `/clear` mechanism.

### `search_session_log` (`src/tools/memory.ts:341-405`)
- **Engine mode, no `kinds` filter → delegates to the turn ledger** (`searchTurnEvents`, BM25-ranked turn summaries with artifact IDs/files/errors; source `"turn_ledger"`, lines 375-384).
- Otherwise → `eventLog.search(..., afterResetBoundary: true)` (386-403), source `"event_log"`.
- Related engine tools in `src/tools/knowledge.ts`: `search_turn_events` (39), `context_summary` (81), `retrieve_artifact` (102, with grep/line/jsonPath filters and identical-retry short-circuit returning just the artifact card), plus `recall`/`remember` for cross-session Cognitive Memory.

**Conclusion:** the full session history is already append-only, durable, and searchable via substring (event log) and BM25 (turn ledger). What does *not* exist is feeding that history to the LLM as appended messages — it is re-rendered into the system prompt each turn instead.

## 7. Existing compaction / summarization / truncation

### Classic-mode auto-compaction — `src/auto-compact.ts` (146 lines)
- `maybeAutoCompactClassic(session, promptTokens, modelId)` (69-138), called at `turn.ts:700`:
  1. `computeContextPressureRatio(promptTokens, contextWindow, reservedOutput)`.
  2. `shouldTriggerAutoCompact` — **hysteresis**: arm at `auto_compact_at` (0.75), disarm below `auto_compact_clear_at` (0.55); `verbatim_only` disables (`src/context-pressure.ts:40-57`; session arming state `src/session.ts:187,1147-1151`).
  3. Takes oldest `compact_chunk_fraction` (0.25) of selectable (non context_action/system_note) uncompressed events after reset boundary (min 4 events).
  4. `session.memoryStore.compressTurns(sessionEvents)` → LLM call (`summarizeTurns`, below) → 1-5 episodic facts stored in Cognitive Memory via `remember`.
  5. `markEventsAsCompressed(...)` + `history_compacted` system_note (114-123); turn.ts then **recompiles** the classic prompt without those events (turn.ts:710-727).
- `formatCompactionBanner` (140-145).

### LLM summarizers — `src/memory/summarizer.ts`
- `extractLearnings(llm, events, surfaced?, opts)` (~line 116): session-end "what did we learn" → 0-5 learnings (fact/preference/decision/pattern/mistake/constraint) with project/global scope; skips content already in AGENTS.md/README.
- `summarizeTurns(llm, events)` (256-320): `TURN_COMPRESSION_PROMPT` → 1-5 key points "to replace the raw turns in the agent's context" — the compaction summarizer.
- `MemoryStore.compressTurns` (`src/memory/store.ts:359-381`); session-end flow at `store.ts:250-360` (`endSession` with combined learnings+usedIds call).
- Summarizer adapters: `src/memory/summarizer-factory.ts` (`NativeSummarizer` over the native LLM subsystem), `openai-summarizer.ts`, `ollama-summarizer.ts`.

### Engine-mode "compaction"
Not history rewriting — **pressure modes** (`normal`/`compact`/`emergency`) degrade rendering: drop >6-turn-old units, shrink checkpoint sections, keep only current-turn artifact cards in emergency (engine-compiler.ts:207-225, 309-342). Telemetry counts `compaction_triggers` on escalation (`telemetry.ts:70-78`).

### Other truncation points

Good — let's lay it out properly. First, one framing correction, then pros/cons.

## What your proposal actually changes

Today, **neither** mode appends cross-turn messages. Every turn, PRAANA rebuilds one big system prompt string (classic: full history re-rendered as text; engine: scored/budgeted selection), and `messages[]` only ever holds the *current* turn's tool loop. So your proposal has two distinct parts:

1. **Transport change** — carry real `user`/`assistant`/`tool_result` messages across turns (prefix-stable, append-only) instead of re-rendering history into the system prompt.
2. **Lifecycle change** — rolling compaction: at some threshold, summarize the oldest chunk, prepend `[summary] + [verbatim recent tail]`, keep the full trail searchable (`search_session_log` / turn ledger / `retrieve_artifact` already exist — this is exactly Cursor's point #2).

## Pros

- **Prompt caching.** This is the big one you didn't mention: a stable appended prefix is cacheable (Anthropic/OpenAI cache on prefix). Rebuilding a curated system prompt every turn *guarantees* cache misses. Cached input is ~10x cheaper and faster. Curation is actively costing you here.
- **Faithfulness.** No digest-extraction loss, no "scoring didn't pick that turn" failures. The model sees exactly what happened — modern long-context models handle this well, which is why Claude Code/opencode/Cursor all converged on append+compact.
- **Simplicity.** The engine pipeline (scoring, bands, density weighting, pressure modes, checkpoints, embedding cache) is ~6k lines. Replacing it with "append + threshold + summarize + search" is maybe ~500 lines using pieces you already have (`computeContextPressureRatio`, `summarizeTurns`, `markEventsAsCompressed`).
- **Loss is recoverable.** Because full history stays in `events.jsonl` and is searchable, compaction degrades gracefully instead of catastrophically.
- **Debuggability.** What was sent = system + history. No more `/why` archaeology.

## Cons

- **Quadratic input growth.** Turn N resends all N-1 turns. Prompt caching fixes *cost* but not *window pressure* — you still hit the limit and must compact well before 128K of stale tool output.
- **Context rot.** Ancient full-fat tool results (big greps, file reads, diffs) dilute attention. This is the engine's actual raison d'être — "lost in the middle" is real, even if modern models tolerate it better.
- **Tool-result bloat.** One `shell` run can dump 64KB into the permanent prefix. Mitigation exists: the engine's artifact store (`ingestToolResult` → inline if ≤400 tokens, else card + `retrieve_artifact`) is *literally* Cursor's "long tool responses → files" pattern. There's also an unwired 64K `serializeToolResult` cap.
- **Mid-session `/model` switching breaks.** Append-only provider-formatted messages don't port cleanly between Anthropic/OpenAI wire formats. Today's text re-rendering makes model switching trivial.
- **You lose the experiment.** PRAANA's thesis is measuring curated vs. plain context (that's what the scorecard is for). Deleting the engine ends that measurement. Worth asking: has the scorecard data actually shown the engine winning? If not, that's evidence for your side.
- **Compaction quality becomes critical.** A bad summary now poisons everything downstream. Needs a strong summarizer prompt + explicit "search the log if the summary lacks detail" instruction.

## Middle-ground worth considering

**Keep the artifact store, delete the curator.** Append verbatim messages, but route large tool results through the existing artifact store so the prefix stays lean and details stay retrievable. Keep state graph (tasks/decisions/constraints) as a *small static* section — it's cheap and genuinely useful. Kill scoring/bands/density/pressure-modes. That gets you ~90% of the simplification with the bloat problem already solved.

Rolling compaction shape: trigger at ~50-60% of window (leave room; compaction itself costs a call), summarize oldest events into a summary stored **as an event in the log** (so resume is lossless), keep tail verbatim, repeat — summaries stack or roll forward.

## Questions before we go deeper

1. **Kill the engine or keep it behind a flag?** It's the project's research centerpiece — is the scorecard evidence strong enough either way to decide?
2. **Real messages vs. text-rendered history?** Real messages unlock caching and tool protocols but complicate `/model` switching and resume. I'd lean real messages.
3. **Keep the artifact store for large tool results?** I'd strongly recommend yes — it's the best defense against prefix bloat and it's already built.
4. **Compaction trigger:** token-fraction threshold (recommended — reuses existing hysteresis code), turn count, or both?

My honest take: the proposal is the right direction — the industry has voted, and PRAANA's existing search/artifact infrastructure means you'd get Cursor's design almost for free. The only thing I'd fight to keep is the artifact store in the loop.

## Assistant (Plan · Qwen3.8 Max · 17.4s)

_Thinking:_

The user is asking for a simple explanation of "real messages vs text-rendered history." Keep it simple, with examples.

Two ways to feed past conversation back to the model:

**Text-rendered history (what PRAANA does today)**
Everything from previous turns is flattened into one big string inside the *system prompt*. The model sees it as plain text:

```
System: You are PRAANA...

<conversation>
User: fix the login bug
PRAANA: I'll check auth.ts
Tool call: read_file({"path":"src/auth.ts"})
Result (read_file): "export function login() {...}"
User: now add tests
</conversation>
```

It's just a transcript pasted into instructions. The API call has only *one* real message: the current input.

**Real messages (what Claude Code / opencode / your proposal)**
History is sent as actual API message objects with proper roles:

```
system: You are PRAANA...
messages: [
  { role: "user",      content: "fix the login bug" },
  { role: "assistant", content: "I'll check auth.ts", tool_calls: [read_file] },
  { role: "tool",      content: "export function login() {...}" },
  { role: "user",      content: "now add tests" }
]
```

**Why it matters:**

| | Text-rendered | Real messages |
|---|---|---|
| Prompt caching | breaks every turn (string changes) | works — prefix is identical, ~10x cheaper reads |
| Model understanding | transcript-like, secondhand | native format models are trained on |
| Tool calls | look like quoted text | proper structured tool_use/tool_result pairs |
| Switching model/provider mid-session | easy — just re-render | tricky — Anthropic and OpenAI wire formats differ |
| Resume | re-render from event log | must reconstruct exact message objects (pairing tool calls with results) |

**Analogy:** text-rendered = emailing someone a copy-pasted chat log. Real messages = adding them live to the group chat. The log works, but the native format is what everything (caching, tool protocols) is optimized for.

## Design: "append mode" (working name)

### Data model
- Canonical history: reuse events.jsonl (already full-fidelity, append-only, fsync). On resume, reconstruct `ConversationMessage[]` from events (user_message → user, agent_message → assistant text, tool_call → assistant tool_use, tool_result → tool result). Actually this is exactly the reconstruction `TurnLedger.migrateFromEvents` does for the ledger; we need a message reconstruction path.
- In memory: `Session.messages: ConversationMessage[]` — the live appended history.

### Per-turn flow
1. Compile: system prompt = frame (static-ish: identity, cwd, AGENTS.md, policy, skill catalog, memory digest, active state if we keep it, compaction summary section) — keep stable for caching; put volatile stuff in messages or at the tail.
2. Append user message to history.
3. Send system + full message history; within-turn tool loop appends assistant/tool messages as it does today.
4. Log events as today (nothing changes).

### Compaction
- Trigger: token ratio threshold — e.g. compute pressure from provider-reported usage (already captured as `usage.input` per step) against (window − reserved output). Arm at ~0.6-0.7, with hysteresis via existing `shouldTriggerAutoCompact` machinery (auto_compact_at exists).
- On trigger: take the oldest chunk of history (e.g. oldest 25-50% of messages, cut at turn boundary), summarize with LLM (`summarizeTurns` exists, or a better rolling summary prompt), produce a `compaction` event in the event log (so resume is lossless), and replace those messages with a single summary user/system message at the head.
- Summary placement: as a `user`-role or `system`-role message right after the system prompt, e.g. "[Conversation summary so far] …". Anthropic allows multiple system blocks; simplest: summary message with role user/assistant pair. Need to keep tool_use/tool_result pairing valid — only cut at turn boundaries (never split a tool call from its result).
- Rolling: next compaction summarizes the oldest chunk + previous summary → new summary (stacking/roll-forward).

### Artifact store integration
- Keep `ingestToolResult`: results >400 tokens → artifact card in the message + `retrieve_artifact` for details. This is already wired into engine mode in turn.ts (1208-1267); in the new mode we wire it into the default path.

### Searchable history
- Already exists: `search_session_log` (event-log substring search, including compressed events), `search_turn_events` (BM25 ledger), `retrieve_artifact`. ### State graph
- Keep tasks/decisions/constraints as a small static section in the system prompt (cheap). Tier management continues to apply.

### Config
- New mode as default: `context_engine.enabled` default becomes `false`? Or a new key. Options: keep `context_engine.enabled` (engine behind flag, default off) and add `append`/`history` config: `[history] compact_at = 0.6`, `compact_chunk_fraction`, etc. Or reuse existing `[compiler]` compaction keys.

### Prompt-cache friendliness
- System frame: remove timestamp/session volatility from the head (move to tail or messages) so the prefix is stable. Skill catalog + memory digest change per session but stable within a session — fine.
- Note: memory digest and active state do change across turns (state gets touched) — those mutations invalidate the cache from that point on. Put them at the tail of the system prompt so at least the big static head + message prefix stay cached? Actually cache works on prefix — a change in the middle of the system prompt invalidates everything after. Order: stable frame first, volatile sections last, then messages.

### Resume
- Reconstruct messages from events.jsonl: replay events → messages, apply compaction events (replace ranges with summaries), respect reset boundaries. State graph checkpoint already gives O(1) state restoration.

### /model switching
- Canonical store is events; convert to provider format per send (drivers already format ConversationMessage[] — actually runLlmStream already canonicalizes; the history we keep is canonical ConversationMessage[]; drivers handle per-provider formatting each time. So switching mostly works; edge case: provider-specific tool call ID format. Keep a fallback: on provider switch mid-session, optionally render history as text once. Maybe don't overengineer; note as a risk.)

### Telemetry
- Scorecard keeps working (measurement_mode already supports classic). Add compaction counters.

### Implementation phases
1. Phase 1: Message-history session model — `Session.messages`, reconstruct from events on resume, append per turn, send via runLlmStream (drop per-turn history re-render). Gate behind a mode flag first.
2. Phase 2: Rolling compaction — threshold trigger, summarizer, compaction event, replacement message.
3. Phase 3: Artifact store integration into the default path + search instructions + caching-friendly system frame ordering.

Locked in: engine stays behind a flag, artifact store stays in the loop, compaction triggered by token-fraction only. Here's the shape of the design:

## Design sketch — "append mode"

**Per turn**
```
[system prompt]                      ← stable prefix (frame, AGENTS.md, skills, memory digest, active state)
[messages...]                        ← real, appended, never re-rendered
  summary msg (only after compaction)
  verbatim history: user / assistant / tool_use / tool_result
  current turn
```
- `Session.messages: ConversationMessage[]` is the live history; `events.jsonl` remains the canonical durable store — resume rebuilds messages from events (the driver layer already converts canonical messages per provider, so `/model` switching mostly works for free).
- Large tool results route through the existing artifact store → inline card in the message, full payload via `retrieve_artifact` (this is the code at `src/turn.ts:1208-1267`, currently engine-only — gets promoted to the default path).

**Compaction (rolling)**
- Trigger: pressure from provider-reported `usage.input` (already captured per step) vs `window − reserved_output`, armed with the existing hysteresis machinery (`computeContextPressureRatio` / `shouldTriggerAutoCompact`).
- Action: cut oldest chunk **at a turn boundary** (never split tool_use/tool_result pairs), summarize via the existing summarizer, write a `compaction` event to `events.jsonl` (lossless resume), replace the chunk with one summary message. Next compaction rolls the old summary into the new one.

**Searchability** — already built: `search_session_log` searches compressed events too, turn ledger gives BM25, artifacts give payload recovery. Just add the system-prompt instruction: *"Older turns are summarized; search before guessing."*

**Cache friendliness** — volatile sections (state, digest) go at the *end* of the system prompt; timestamp/session-id move out of the prefix head so the cached prefix survives turn-to-turn.

**Phases**
1. Session message model: append + resume rebuild + send (flag-gated)
2. Rolling compaction + `compaction` event
3. Artifact store promotion + cache-stable system frame + search instruction
4. Default flip: append mode = default, engine = opt-in flag, scorecard keeps measuring both

## Remaining questions

1. **Classic mode's fate** — the new mode supersedes it. Delete classic, or keep it as the fallback path? (I'd delete — one less code path; append mode *is* the fallback when engine is off.)
2. **Threshold** — arm compaction at what fraction? Existing classic uses 0.75; I'd use **0.6** to leave room for within-turn tool-loop growth before the summary call completes.
3. **Chunk size** — oldest 25% of messages per compaction (matches existing `compact_chunk_fraction`), or a bigger 50%? Bigger = fewer compactions, lossier per step.
4. **Flag naming** — engine becomes opt-in via `context_engine.enabled = false` by default, or do you want an explicit `[history] mode = "append" | "engine"` style switch?

# Plan: History mode (append + rolling compaction + searchable trail)

## Decisions locked
- New **history mode** is the default; engine stays opt-in behind a flag; classic is deleted.
- Artifact store stays in the loop for large tool results.
- Compaction trigger: token-fraction only, **arm at 0.6**, **compact oldest 50%** per event, turn-boundary cuts.

## 1. Config surface (`src/config.ts`, `src/types.ts`)
```toml
[history]
mode = "append"        # "append" | "engine"  (default "append")
compact_at = 0.6       # fraction of (window − reserved_output)
clear_at = 0.45        # disarm hysteresis (reuse shouldTriggerAutoCompact)
compact_chunk_fraction = 0.5
```
`context_engine.enabled` becomes an alias: `mode="engine"` implies it. Engine scoring/pressure knobs stay for engine mode only.

## 2. Message model (`src/session.ts`, `src/turn.ts`)
- New `Session.messages: ConversationMessage[]` (canonical type already exists, `src/llm/types.ts:29`).
- Per turn: append user message → send `systemPrompt + Session.messages` → append assistant/tool_result messages during the tool loop (replaces the fresh-per-turn `history` at `src/turn.ts:803`). Events still logged exactly as today — `events.jsonl` remains the canonical durable store.
- **Resume:** rebuild `Session.messages` from events after the last reset boundary: `user_message`→user, `agent_message`→assistant(+toolCalls), `tool_call`/`tool_result` pairs→assistant toolCalls + tool_result. A `compaction` event replaces its summarized event-id range with the stored summary message (see §3). State graph O(1) checkpoint restore is untouched.

## 3. Rolling compaction (`src/history-compact.ts` — new, ~250 lines)
- **Trigger:** provider-reported `usage.input` (already captured per step) / `(window − reserved_output)` ≥ 0.6, armed/disarmed via existing hysteresis (`src/context-pressure.ts`). Fallback to `estimateTokens` before first usage arrives. Check at turn start and after each tool step.
- **Action:** select oldest 50% of messages, cut only at turn boundaries (never split toolCalls/tool_results), summarize via existing summarizer (`summarizeTurns`, `src/memory/summarizer.ts` — prompt adjusted for rolling summaries: fold prior summary into new one), then:
  - append `compaction` event to `events.jsonl` with `{first_event_id, last_event_id, summary}` — lossless resume, and compressed events stay searchable;
  - replace the chunk with one summary message (`role: "user"` with `[Summary of earlier conversation]` prefix) right after system prompt.
- Summarizer failure → skip compaction this turn, retry next (never drop messages without a summary).

## 4. Artifact store + search wiring (`src/turn.ts:1208-1267`, `src/context-engine/index.ts`)
- History mode still opens a **slim ContextEngine**: ArtifactStore + TurnLedger + scorecard only (no checkpoints/extraction/scoring). The artifact-card substitution path (`ingestToolResult` → inline ≤400 tokens, else card + `retrieve_artifact`) moves from engine-only to the shared path.
- `search_session_log` / `search_turn_events` / `retrieve_artifact` registered in history mode (currently gated by `classicMode` in `src/tools/index.ts:63-71`).
- System frame gets one new instruction: *"Older turns are summarized. Use search_session_log / retrieve_artifact to recover details before assuming they're lost."*

## 5. Cache-stable system frame (`src/compile-classic.ts` → replaced by `src/compile-history.ts`)
Order, most-stable first: identity/policy/AGENTS.md → skills catalog → memory digest → active state → compaction/search instructions. Volatile bits (timestamps) move to the end or into messages, so the cached prefix survives turn-to-turn. State graph (tasks/decisions/constraints) stays as a small static section — recommended to keep; it's cheap and orthogonal to transport. Push back if you want it gone.

## 6. Classic deletion list
`src/compile-classic.ts`, `src/auto-compact.ts` (keep pressure helpers in `context-pressure.ts`), classic branches in `src/turn.ts` (467-730, 1445-1542), `classicMode` plumbing in `src/tools/index.ts`, `tests/compile-classic.test.ts`, `"classic"` in `src/context-display.ts:13` → `"history"`.

## 7. Tests
- Resume → message reconstruction (incl. tool-call pairing, compaction replay, reset boundary)
- Compaction: trigger threshold, turn-boundary cuts, rolling summary fold-in, disarm hysteresis
- Artifact substitution in history mode; cache-prefix stability (system prompt prefix unchanged across turns)
- Config parsing for `[history]`; engine mode regression untouched

## 8. Phases
1. Message model + resume rebuild (flag-gated, engine still default during dev)
2. Compaction + `compaction` event
3. Slim ContextEngine + artifact/search promotion + cache-stable frame
4. Default flip, classic deletion, AGENTS.md/docs update

**One open item:** keep state-graph tools (`create_task`/`decide`/`add_constraint`) in history mode as a small static section — recommended yes. Sound good to start with Phase 1?

can you review the plan. what kind of problems can we face with this also review the below plan from someone else

### The Intuition: Why You Are Right About the Problem

  Your core intuition is spot on: tool outputs are the #1 cause of context bloat and degraded agent reasoning.

  • A single git diff, read_file, or npm test can easily dump 2,000–10,000 tokens into the conversation history.
  • If you append all raw tool outputs across multiple turns, 80% of your context window becomes stale logs and code listings that the
  model read 5 turns ago and no longer needs.
  • This bloat drowns out the user's instructions (needle-in-a-haystack problem) and burns context limits rapidly.

  However, how and when you summarize or separate tool outputs introduces several critical traps.
  ──────
  ### The Traps & Practical Problems

  #### 1. The Hard API Protocol Constraint
  All modern tool-calling APIs (Anthropic Messages API, OpenAI Chat Completions, Gemini Function Calling) enforce strict message schema
  validation:

  • If an assistant message contains tool_calls (or tool_use), the immediate next message must be a tool (or tool_result) message
  containing the matching tool_call_id.
  • If you don't provide the tool result, or replace it with a generic summary or assistant message, the API returns an immediate HTTP 400
  Validation Error.
  • Implication: During the turn, the raw tool call and its result must exist in the conversation loop for the provider API to accept
  subsequent steps.
  #### 2. Loss of Exact Precision (The Hallucination Trap)
  When an LLM summarizes a tool output (especially code or compiler errors), it naturally abstracts details:

  • Code reads: An LLM summary might say: "The file defines an authentication middleware and imports JWT utils."
      • But when the agent subsequently needs to edit the file using edit_file, it needs the exact line contents, indentation, and function
  • Test / Build errors: A summary might say: "Tests failed with a type error."
      signatures. If it only has a summary, it will hallucinate the exact syntax and edit_file will fail with string mismatch errors.
      • But the agent needs the exact file, line number, column, and TypeScript error code (TS2345: Argument of type...) to pinpoint the
      fix.
  #### 3. Latency & Cost Explosion (Summarizing Every Tool Call)
  • If you invoke a separate LLM call to summarize every tool call, a turn with 4 tool calls (find_files → read_file → edit_file → bun
  test) now requires 4 extra LLM roundtrips.
  • At ~1.0–2.5 seconds per summary call, turn latency doubles or triples (an extra 4–10 seconds of user waiting), and you burn thousands
  of extra tokens just to summarize small or transient outputs.
  #### 4. The Prefix Prompt-Caching Killer

  Modern frontier models (Claude 3.5/3.7, GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0, DeepSeek) use Prefix Prompt Caching:
  • If turn history is appended monotonically, the prefix of previous turns remains byte-for-byte identical. Providers cache this prefix,
  giving you 90% token cost discounts and 3x–5x faster Time-To-First-Token (TTFT).
  • If you rewrite or summarize previous turns on every single turn, you invalidate the prompt cache on every turn, making the session
  significantly more expensive and sluggish.
  ──────
  ### The Better, Practical Design: A 3-Stage Hybrid

  We can achieve your exact goal (preventing tool outputs from bloating the context window) while avoiding all of the traps above by
  separating Intra-Turn Execution from Cross-Turn History.

    flowchart TD
        subgraph Turn_N ["During Turn N (Intra-Turn Execution)"]
            TC["Model invokes Tool Call"]
            TO["Tool Output Produced"]

            TO -->|Size <= 800 tokens| TR_INLINE["Inline verbatim tool_result\n(Full fidelity for next step)"]
            TO -->|Size > 800 tokens| TR_SPILL["Spill full output to session file\n(~/.praana/sessions/id/tool_outputs/call_123.log)"]
            TR_SPILL --> TR_PREVIEW["Return Head/Tail preview + File link\nin tool_result"]
        end

        subgraph Turn_N_Plus_1 ["Between Turns (Cross-Turn Retention)"]
            TR_INLINE --> COND{"Turn Finished?\nContext Pressure > 70%?"}
            TR_PREVIEW --> COND

            COND -->|Recent 3 Turns| KEEP["Keep verbatim\n(Preserves Prompt Cache)"]
            COND -->|Older Turns 1..N-3| COMPACT["Batch Compact into Episodic Summary\n(Strip stale tool outputs to 1-line notes)"]
        end

        subgraph Dynamic_Recovery ["Searchable History (Zero Info Loss)"]
            COMPACT -. "Full details retained in" .-> EL["events.jsonl & tool_outputs/"]
            AGENT["Agent needs historical details?"] -. "Calls search_session_log or read_file" .-> EL
        end
  #### Stage 1: During the Turn — Spill Large Outputs to Files (Cursor Pattern #1)

  • For tool outputs under a threshold (e.g. 800 tokens / ~3,000 chars): pass them directly in tool_result so the model has 100% precision
  for immediate edits and reasoning.
  • For tool outputs over 800 tokens (e.g. huge git diff, full test run, or 1,000-line file read):
      • Do not make an extra LLM call to summarize.
      • Automatically write the raw output to a dedicated file: ~/.praana/sessions/<id>/tool_outputs/<toolCallId>.log.
      • Return a deterministic preview in tool_result:
        [Output truncated: 480 lines. Full output saved to: ~/.praana/sessions/s1/tool_outputs/call_123.log]
        --- First 15 lines ---
        ...
        --- Last 25 lines ---
        ...
        (Use read_file or grep on the log file if specific intermediate output is needed)

  • Why this works: Zero LLM summarization latency, zero extra cost, satisfies API tool-result validation, and immediately stops massive
  bloat.

  #### Stage 2: Aging Cross-Turn Tool Results (Pruning Stale Calls)

  • When Turn 1 completes and Turn 2 begins, Turn 1's tool results are now historical.
  • Instead of keeping raw 800-token file reads from Turn 1 in Turn 5's active context:
      • For turns older than K turns (e.g. older than the last 2–3 turns), we can deterministically collapse completed tool results into
      compact markers:
      Tool call: read_file("src/turn.ts") -> [Read 150 lines (cached)]
      • The model only needs to know what was done; if it needs the content again, it reads it or checks the file.


  #### Stage 3: Rolling Compaction (Cursor Pattern #2)

  • When total conversation tokens cross the watermark (e.g. 70% of the model's window):
      • Run one single batch LLM summarization on turns 1…N - K.
      • Compress those older turns into a clean episodic brief (user intent, decisions, files modified, active constraints).
      • Add a pointer: "Full history preserved in events.jsonl. Use search_session_log to look up exact details."
      • This keeps the last 3 turns completely intact (protecting prompt caching) while shedding 80% of the token weight from turns that
      occurred 20 minutes ago.

  ──────
  ### Comparison of Approaches

   Criteria                 | Summarize every tool call via LLM       | Current Classic (Du… | Proposed Hybrid (Spill-to-file + Rolling C…
  --------------------------|-----------------------------------------|----------------------|---------------------------------------------
   API Protocol Compliance  | ❌ Fails (breaks tool_use/tool_result   | Passes               | Passes
                            | pairs unless faked)                     |                      |
   Precision on Code Edits  | ❌ Poor (summaries lose exact           | Full precision       | Full precision for active turn
                            | lines/syntax)                           |                      |
   Per-Tool Latency         | ❌ Slow (+1–2s per tool call)           | Fast (0ms extra)     | Fast (0ms extra, deterministic file write)
   Prompt Cache Hit Rate    | ❌ Zero (mutates prefix constantly)     | ⚠️ Moderate          | High (prefix remains stable for K turns)
   Protection Against Bloat | High                                    | ❌ None (eventually  | High
                            |                                         | crashes window)      |
   Recoverability           | ⚠️ Hard (summaries lose data)           | ❌ N/A               | Full (via search_session_log & tool log
                            |                                         |                      | files)

91:   }

94:     return { compacted: false, eventsCompacted: 0, factsStored: 0, pressureRatio };

26: /** Prompt fill ratio against usable context (window minus reserved output). */
27: export function computeContextPressureRatio(
28:   usedTokens: number,
29:   contextWindowTokens: number,
30:   reservedOutputTokens = 0,
31: ): number {

46:     resolveCompactionConfig(config);

48: 
49:   let nextArmed = armed;
50:   if (pressureRatio >= autoCompactAt) nextArmed = true;
51:   else if (pressureRatio < autoCompactClearAt) nextArmed = false;
52:

<task_result>
# Executive assessment

The proposed redesign is directionally correct and substantially better than the current classic path, but it is not safe to implement as “persist the existing events, reconstruct `ConversationMessage[]`, and compact at 60%.” Three prerequisites are blocking:

1. The durable transcript must become protocol-lossless, including provider-specific opaque reasoning/thought data.
2. Context admission and compaction must run before every provider request, including every tool-loop step and fallback-provider retry.
3. Compaction must be an atomic projection change over committed outer turns, never a destructive side effect of summarization.

Completed historical tool-call/result pairs can be removed for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and Bedrock, but only as complete protocol groups within complete outer turns. No retained message may refer to a removed call, and the currently active tool cycle must remain intact.

The alternative proposal should not be adopted as the primary design. Its immediate, deterministic preview is useful, but per-call files duplicate the existing artifact machinery, age-based rewriting repeatedly damages prompt-cache reuse, and “summarize everything except three turns at 70%” is too late and too coarse.

---

# Findings, ordered by severity

## Critical 1: The current canonical message type is not protocol-lossless enough for durable reconstruction

PRAANA’s normalized message model flattens an assistant response into one text string, one optional thinking string/signature, and a list of tool calls:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm/types.ts:5-25`
- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm/types.ts:28-39`

That is adequate for some simple Chat Completions calls, but it cannot faithfully represent all native-driver responses.

### Provider implications

| Provider | What a retained tool cycle must preserve | Current state |
|---|---|---|
| OpenAI Chat Completions | Assistant `tool_calls`, exact IDs, one result per ID, call/result ordering | Mostly representable. The formatter correctly emits assistant calls and `role:"tool"` results at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm/drivers/openai.ts:259-280`. |
| OpenAI Responses | All response output items needed by the next request, including reasoning items for reasoning models, function-call `call_id`, arguments, and outputs | Not representable. The driver reduces output to text plus function calls and reconstructs only those at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm/drivers/responses.ts:133-193` and `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm/drivers/responses.ts:231-250`. OpenAI explicitly requires reasoning items returned alongside tool calls to be passed back for reasoning models. |
| Anthropic | Ordered content blocks, all `tool_use` IDs, following `tool_result` blocks, and unmodified thinking/signature blocks where required | Partially representable. Anthropic signatures are captured at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm/drivers/anthropic.ts:145-171`, but reconstruction reorders content as thinking, text, then all tools at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm/drivers/anthropic.ts:292-322`. Parallel results are emitted as separate user messages at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm/drivers/anthropic.ts:323-335` rather than one grouped result block. |
| Gemini | Ordered model parts, function calls/responses, provider-supplied IDs where present, and thought signatures | Not protocol-lossless. The driver invents random call IDs at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm/drivers/google.ts:171-180`, does not capture a thought signature, and reconstructs only text/function calls at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm/drivers/google.ts:241-260`. Newer Gemini tool workflows require thought signatures to be echoed. |
| Bedrock Converse | `toolUseId`, all corresponding `toolResult` blocks, result status where supported, and provider reasoning/signature/redacted blocks | Tool IDs/results are representable at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm/drivers/bedrock.ts:263-290`, but reasoning is flattened to text at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm/drivers/bedrock.ts:138-160` and then omitted from reconstructed assistant content at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm/drivers/bedrock.ts:263-277`. |

`runLlmStream()` also normalizes historical assistant content by extracting only text and tool blocks, losing arbitrary content-part order and unknown provider data:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:121-173`

### Can completed pairs be removed?

Yes. These APIs are stateless with respect to the supplied message array unless a provider-managed conversation ID is being used. Old call IDs do not have to remain globally present after the entire old interaction has been removed.

The safe cut is:

```text
[compacted complete outer turns]
SUMMARY EPOCH
User N
Assistant/tool-call step N.1
Tool results for every call in N.1
Assistant/tool-call step N.2
Tool results for every call in N.2
Terminal assistant response for N
User N+1
```

The unsafe cases are:

- Removing a tool call but keeping its result.
- Removing one result from a parallel batch.
- Cutting after an assistant tool request but before its results.
- Cutting between tool-loop steps in the current outer turn.
- Retaining an Anthropic/Gemini/Bedrock reasoning block without its required opaque signature.
- Reconstructing an OpenAI Responses reasoning tool cycle from text and function calls alone.

### Required change

Use a richer canonical representation:

- Ordered assistant content blocks, not combined strings.
- Stable `turnId`, `stepId`, `messageSeq`, provider, API and model.
- Exact tool-call/result association.
- The exact deterministic result string sent back to the provider.
- An opaque provider-state field for thought signatures, reasoning items, encrypted/redacted blocks and response item IDs.
- A provider adapter that decides whether opaque blocks may be replayed after a model/provider switch.

“Canonical” should mean lossless for protocol semantics, not merely a common text/tool abstraction.

---

## Critical 2: Existing events cannot reliably reconstruct a valid canonical transcript on resume

The current event log is an audit/UI structure, not a provider transcript.

### Missing assistant tool-step messages

Each model step is placed only into the in-memory `history`:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:1009-1019`

The event log receives:

- Tool calls at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:1065-1074`
- Tool results at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:1294-1298`
- One concatenated, terminal `agent_message` only after the whole outer turn at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:1409-1414`

Consequently, the log loses:

- Assistant text accompanying each tool call.
- Per-step assistant boundaries.
- Raw tool argument JSON.
- Thinking and signatures.
- Finish reasons and provider output item identities.
- The exact result representation sent to the next request.
- Whether a result was an artifact card, a retrieval payload, or an inline result.

The event stores the post-hook result object, while the provider may have received a distilled artifact card in `promptResultText`:

- Artifact conversion: `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:1165-1267`
- Provider history insertion: `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:1285-1292`
- Different event payload: `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:1294-1298`

### Interrupted and concurrent calls create dangling tails

All calls in a parallel batch are logged before execution starts:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:1065-1076`

They are then executed through `Promise.all()`:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:1078-1142`

Results are appended afterward, in original order:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:1160-1163`
- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:1294-1298`

A crash can therefore leave:

- Calls logged but no tools executed.
- Calls logged and side effects performed, but no results logged.
- A subset of result events persisted.
- No terminal assistant message and no explicit turn-commit marker.

The interruption path appends only a generic interruption note and a synthetic terminal assistant message:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:1492-1502`

It does not resolve every outstanding call with an error result. Replaying that tail as native messages would be invalid.

### Current migration pairing is unsafe for parallel same-name calls

The turn-ledger migration ignores `toolCallId` and pairs results to pending calls by tool name:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/context-engine/turn-ledger.ts:33-61`

Two parallel calls to `read_file`, `shell`, or another identical tool can be associated with the wrong arguments. The migrated ledger also omits normal result text from its tool records.

### A partially written final JSON line can hide the whole log

`syncCache()` parses the entire JSONL in one expression and replaces the cache with `[]` on any parse error:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/event-log.ts:124-133`

A truncated final line after process termination can therefore make every prior valid event appear absent.

### Required change

Introduce provider-transcript events written as the source of truth:

1. `turn_started`
2. Complete `assistant_step` with ordered blocks and provider state
3. `tool_batch_started`
4. One durable result per call
5. `tool_batch_completed`
6. Terminal `assistant_step`
7. `turn_committed`

On resume:

- Replay committed turns only.
- Treat an incomplete tail as recovery evidence, not ordinary history.
- Never re-execute an uncertain side effect automatically.
- Tell the next model/user which calls may have completed without durable results.
- Parse the longest valid JSONL prefix and quarantine only a malformed trailing line.
- For legacy logs, compact them into a legacy transcript summary rather than synthesizing supposedly exact native tool messages.

---

## Critical 3: A 60% turn-level trigger alone cannot prevent context-limit failures

Sixty percent is a reasonable soft watermark, but it is not a safety boundary.

### Context can grow dramatically inside one outer turn

PRAANA can perform up to 25 model/tool rounds by default:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/types.ts:406-409`
- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:810-810`
- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:929-935`

The current compaction check runs once before the first provider request:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:682-727`

Each subsequent assistant response and tool batch enlarges the in-memory history, but there is no request admission check before the next step.

Even with artifacts:

- Errors are always kept inline regardless of size at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/context-engine/artifact-store.ts:210-212`.
- A large current user message or assistant response is not handled by the artifact store.
- Many individually sub-threshold results can exceed the remaining budget in aggregate.
- One active outer turn may itself be larger than the 40% headroom.

### There is currently no output reserve

The default is zero:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/config.ts:65-76`

Runtime models default to an 8,192-token output allowance:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm.ts:240-254`

Anthropic may raise `max_tokens` above that to accommodate thinking:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm/drivers/anthropic.ts:40-56`

A 60% input threshold does not account correctly for a 12K reasoning/output allowance on a 32K or 64K model.

### Current estimates omit structured tool schemas

`compiledPrompt` and `messages` are passed separately from `tools`:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:196-212`

The compiler’s token total counts only its assembled text. Although `toolSchemas` is passed into `buildSystemFrame()`, the function does not render or count them:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/compiler.ts:365-445`

Provider tool definitions count against context and can be large.

### Provider usage cannot be the sole trigger

Usage arrives after a successful request, so it cannot protect that request. It is also inconsistent:

- Some OpenAI-compatible providers disable streaming usage at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/provider-registry.ts:186-208`.
- Anthropic’s `input_tokens` excludes cached creation/read tokens, while PRAANA emits those separately at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm/drivers/anthropic.ts:138-144` and `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm/drivers/anthropic.ts:203-213`.
- `runLlmStream()` nevertheless publishes `latestContextTokens: event.usage.input` at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:244-251`, which can severely understate actual Anthropic context occupancy.
- Bedrock parses only `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, and `totalTokens`; it ignores cache-read/write fields at `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/llm/drivers/bedrock.ts:181-192`.

### Fallback models are not re-admitted against their window

Switching to a fallback refreshes the context window and constructs the new model, but does not recompile or compact the request:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:875-887`

A prompt valid for a 200K primary can immediately fail against a 64K fallback.

### Required change

Run admission control before every provider call:

```text
system + tools + retained messages + current in-flight tool cycle
+ requested output/reasoning reserve + safety margin <= context window
```

Use:

- Provider token counting where available.
- Otherwise a conservative estimator over the actual wire representation, including schemas and framing.
- Provider usage only as post-call calibration.
- A normalized `totalContextInputTokens`, distinct from billable uncached input.
- Re-admission after every provider/model/reasoning-effort change.

Recommended policy:

- Soft compact trigger: approximately 55–60% of usable context.
- Target after compaction: approximately 35–40%.
- Hard admission ceiling: `window - actualOutputReserve - safetyMargin`.
- Safety margin: at least 2K tokens and preferably a percentage of the window.
- Check again after each tool batch.

---

## High 4: Compaction must be atomic, token-targeted and independent of Cognitive Memory

The current compaction path demonstrates several failure modes the redesign must avoid.

### Existing cuts are event-count based, not turn-safe

The current algorithm takes a fraction of filtered events:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/auto-compact.ts:97-106`

Its own test approves compressing exactly three events from three two-event turns, leaving the second user message without its response:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/tests/auto-compact.test.ts:101-105`

The redesign’s complete-turn requirement fixes this only if “turn” means the entire outer user turn, not one model/tool step.

### Current compaction can discard history without a replacement

The sequence is:

1. Ask Cognitive Memory to extract facts.
2. Mark source events compressed.
3. Continue using the existing session digest.

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/auto-compact.ts:110-123`

`compressTurns()` returns zero if no summarizer exists:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/memory/store.ts:355-377`

Yet the caller still marks the events compressed. Even when facts are stored successfully, `session.digest` is not refreshed before recompiling; the second compile reuses the old digest:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:710-726`

Thus current-session context can simply disappear. Session-history compaction should not be implemented as cross-session memory extraction.

### “Oldest 50%” needs a token definition

Fifty percent by turn count can:

- Remove very little if recent turns are huge.
- Remove almost everything if one early turn is huge.
- Fail to reach the low watermark.
- Consume a still-active decision merely because it is old.

Select the oldest complete turns by token mass until projected occupancy reaches the target. Preserve a minimum recent-turn floor, but do not assume three turns fit.

### The summarization request may not fit

The current summarizer accepts an unbounded transcript; user and assistant messages are included in full:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/memory/summarizer.ts:89-103`
- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/memory/summarizer.ts:255-269`

The compaction model can differ from the active model and has a fixed provider-specific default:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/memory/summarizer-factory.ts:13-26`

`NativeSummarizer.complete()` also ignores the supplied timeout and does not pass an abort signal:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/memory/summarizer-factory.ts:53-69`

A synchronous pre-request compaction can therefore hang or exceed the summarizer model’s window.

### Required change

A compaction record should be append-only and activation should be transactional:

```text
history_compaction {
  epoch,
  source_start_event,
  source_end_event,
  source_hash,
  summary,
  artifact_refs,
  generated_by,
  created_at
}
```

Activation invariants:

- Generate and validate the summary first.
- Verify that the source range/hash still matches.
- Persist and fsync the new compaction event.
- Only then select the new projection.
- On crash or summarizer failure, continue using the old projection.
- Never mark source events hidden solely because the summarizer returned an empty or malformed result.

For rolling compaction, merge the previous summary epoch with newly retired turns instead of repeatedly re-summarizing the entire history.

## High 5: The existing artifact store is preferable to per-call files, but it is not yet a durable general history store

The artifact system already provides most of what per-call files would attempt to add:

- Session-bound IDs and content hashes: `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/context-engine/artifact-store.ts:33-44`
- Raw text, token count, provenance and fidelity in SQLite: `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/context-engine/db.ts:14-34`
- Session ownership checks: `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/context-engine/artifact-store.ts:383-395`
- Line slicing, regex filtering and JSON extraction: `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/context-engine/artifact-store.ts:398-439`
- A retrievable artifact card: `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/context-engine/summarize.ts:4-17`

Creating a separate file for every call would add another reference type, another cleanup mechanism and another access-control surface.

### Current duplication

The same post-redaction output is commonly stored:

1. In `events.jsonl` as a full result object: `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:1294-1298`
2. In `context_artifacts.raw_text`: `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/context-engine/db.ts:334-373`

A per-call file would become a third copy.

### Current artifact lifetime is not aligned with an “exact historical retrieval” promise

Non-lossless artifacts are deleted according to turn TTL:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/context-engine/db.ts:425-442`

The deletion query is not scoped by `session_id`. Because the database is shared, maintenance from a long-running session can evict summarizable artifacts belonging to another session based on incomparable session-local turn numbers.

Conversely, `read_file` artifacts are marked lossless and never TTL-evicted:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/context-engine/artifact-store.ts:327-345`
- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/context-engine/db.ts:434-439`

That creates unbounded persistent growth across completed sessions.

### Artifact storage is coupled to engine mode

Artifacts are ingested only when `session.contextEngine` exists:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/turn.ts:1188-1268`

`retrieve_artifact` exists only when a context engine exists:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/tools/knowledge.ts:100-199`

The context engine itself is initialized only through the existing `[context_engine]` mode:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/session.ts:1612-1665`

If canonical history becomes the default and engine mode becomes optional, the artifact store must be extracted into a mode-independent service.

### Security and permissions

Post-tool-call redaction runs before event/artifact persistence:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/hooks/index.ts:112-126`
- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/hooks/handlers/redact.ts:10-17`

Per-call files must likewise store the post-redaction canonical result, never raw pre-hook output. The redactor is best-effort and stops walking at depth eight:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/redact/secrets.ts:5-22`
- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/redact/secrets.ts:51-72`

Session directories and event files currently rely on process umask rather than explicitly enforcing `0700`/`0600`:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/event-log.ts:94-102`

The credential store demonstrates the safer atomic and restrictive pattern:

- `/home/amit/projects/praana/src/credentials.ts:148-167`

### Recommendation

Keep one artifact/blob abstraction:

- Store the deterministic, post-redaction result string once.
- Put an artifact reference and immutable preview in the canonical tool result.
- Index the full blob text for search.
- Retain blobs for at least as long as their session history.
- Use per-session storage or fix all shared-DB TTL queries to include session identity.
- Add explicit session retention/deletion policy.
- Enforce restrictive directory and file permissions.
- Do not expose raw filesystem paths to the model; retain session-scoped `retrieve_artifact(id, ...)`.
