A line-by-line rewrite would preserve obsolete architecture and create a large semantic verification burden.\n+\n+Rust v2 must instead preserve contracts that still matter and deliberately replace the rest.\n+\n+### Preserve\n+\n+- Provider wire correctness, including streaming and tool calls.\n+- Safety-hook behavior and ordering.\n+- Shell process-tree cancellation.\n+- Credential and secret-handling expectations.\n+- Config source precedence where retained by the v2 config spec.\n+- StateGraph semantics that remain useful.\n+- Lossless source artifacts and filtered retrieval.\n+- Headless operation and Harbor compatibility.\n+- Interactive behavior while the TypeScript UI remains the client.\n+\n+### Replace\n+\n+- Per-turn reconstruction of cross-turn history into a system-prompt string.\n+- The current reduced event log as the only resume substrate.\n+- The coupling between Cognitive Memory, embeddings, skills, artifacts, scorecard, and the context engine.\n+- The compression checkpoint sidecar as authoritative state.\n+- The concrete `MemoryStore` dependency throughout `Session` and tools.\n+- Duplicate transcript representations that can disagree.\n+\n+### Delete rather than port\n+\n+- `src/compile-classic.ts`.\n+- `src/auto-compact.ts` behavior that writes old turns into Cognitive Memory.\n+- Classic-mode branching and naming.\n+- Old session/database migrations.\n+- Default ONNX embedding setup.\n+- N-API packaging after the TypeScript client is retired.\n+- Bun-specific global package installation as an initial v2 requirement.\n+\n+AI-assisted implementation reduces typing and translation cost. It does not reduce the need for wire fixtures, crash tests, security checks, or semantic comparison. Compilation is necessary but never sufficient acceptance evidence.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 3. Target Runtime Architecture\n+\n+```text\n+User / headless caller / temporary TypeScript UI\n+                    |\n+                    v\n+              Rust application\n+                    |\n+          +---------+---------+\n+          |                   |\n+          v                   v\n+   Session controller      UI event sink\n+          |\n+          v\n+   Turn orchestrator\n+          |\n+          +--> request admission\n+          +--> provider adapter\n+          +--> tool/safety pipeline\n+          +--> canonical event append\n+          +--> logical history projection\n+          +--> artifact/session search\n+          +--> StateGraph projection\n+          +--> compaction projection\n+          +--> optional memory plugin\n+```\n+\n+The core separates storage from what the model sees.\n+\n+```text\n+Canonical event history\n+  Every accepted or failed attempt, tool execution, state change,\n+  compaction, reset, model switch, and supersession\n+                    |\n+                    v\n+Logical accepted conversation\n+  Only accepted user/assistant messages and protocol-complete tool groups\n+                    |\n+                    v\n+Model-visible request\n+  Stable system/tool prefix + bounded handoff + current StateGraph\n+  + recent accepted real messages + current in-flight tool cycle\n+```\n+\n+Append-only describes the durable record. It does not require feeding failed, superseded, compacted, or protocol-incompatible records to the model.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 4. Rust Workspace\n+\n+Keep the initial crate structure small.\n+\n+```text\n+crates/\n+  praana-native-core/   # pure Rust tree-sitter, search, project detection\n+  praana-natives/       # temporary N-API wrapper; deleted at final cutover\n+  praana-core/          # runtime, providers, history, tools, state, plugins\n+  praana-cli/           # executable, config, headless, temporary IPC, later TUI\n+```\n+\n+### `praana-native-core`\n+\n+- Move reusable logic from `crates/praana-natives/src/` behind Rust-native types.\n+- Keep N-API annotations and JavaScript DTOs out of this crate.\n+- Search and parsing functions accept already-validated paths and bounded options.\n+- Do not include ONNX in the default feature set.\n+\n+### `praana-natives`\n+\n+- Temporarily depend on `praana-native-core`.\n+- Preserve the current TypeScript application's native API while the UI bridge exists.\n+- Contain only N-API conversion, version checks, and errors.\n+- Delete after the TypeScript application is retired.\n+\n+### `praana-core`\n+\n+Use modules before creating more crates:\n+\n+```text\n+src/\n+  protocol/\n+  history/\n+  provider/\n+  artifacts/\n+  state/\n+  tools/\n+  hooks/\n+  memory/\n+  telemetry/\n+  config/\n+```\n+\n+Create a new crate only for a real binary, plugin, compilation, or API boundary.\n+\n+### `praana-cli`\n+\n+- Produce the `praana` executable.\n+- Own command parsing and process exit behavior.\n+- Initially provide `praana run`, `praana doctor`, and session resume commands.\n+- Provide a temporary framed JSONL IPC mode for OpenTUI.\n+- Add Ratatui only after the headless core and bridge are stable.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 5. Canonical Event Protocol\n+\n+### Envelope\n+\n+Every event is one JSON object on one line.\n+\n+```rust\n+struct EventEnvelope {\n+    schema_version: u32,\n+    event_id: Ulid,\n+    session_id: Ulid,\n+    sequence: u64,\n+    timestamp_ms: i64,\n+    turn_id: Option<Ulid>,\n+    attempt_id: Option<Ulid>,\n+    event: CanonicalEvent,\n+}\n+```\n+\n+`sequence` is monotonic within a session and is the replay order. Timestamps are metadata, not ordering authority.\n+\n+### Event taxonomy\n+\n+```rust\n+enum CanonicalEvent {\n+    SessionStarted(SessionStarted),\n+    UserMessageAccepted(UserMessageAccepted),\n+    TurnStarted(TurnStarted),\n+    AssistantAttemptStarted(AssistantAttemptStarted),\n+    AssistantAttemptFailed(AssistantAttemptFailed),\n+    AssistantStepAccepted(AssistantStepAccepted),\n+    AttemptSuperseded(AttemptSuperseded),\n+    ToolExecutionStarted(ToolExecutionStarted),\n+    ToolExecutionFinished(ToolExecutionFinished),\n+    ToolBatchCompleted(ToolBatchCompleted),\n+    TurnCommitted(TurnCommitted),\n+    TurnInterrupted(TurnInterrupted),\n+    StateChanged(StateChanged),\n+    HistoryCompacted(HistoryCompacted),\n+    ModelChanged(ModelChanged),\n+    ResetBoundary(ResetBoundary),\n+    SystemNote(SystemNote),\n+}\n+```\n+\n+### Attempt rules\n+\n+- Provider retries always receive a new `attempt_id`.\n+- Partial streamed output belongs to an attempt, not the accepted conversation.\n+- An assistant step becomes model-visible history only after `AssistantStepAccepted` is durable.\n+- `AttemptSuperseded` identifies the accepted replacement for a failed or abandoned attempt.\n+- The UI may optimistically render streaming deltas, but it must rewind them if the attempt fails or is superseded.\n+- Failed partial output remains available for audit and debugging but is excluded from normal model history.\n+\n+### Tool execution rules\n+\n+- `AssistantStepAccepted` contains the tool calls exactly as accepted from the provider adapter.\n+- Persist `ToolExecutionStarted` before invoking each tool.\n+- Persist `ToolExecutionFinished` only after the post-tool hook pipeline and artifact handling complete.\n+- Associate parallel calls and results by tool-call ID, never by tool name or array position alone.\n+- Persist `ToolBatchCompleted` only when every accepted call has a durable result.\n+- A crash after `ToolExecutionStarted` but before `ToolExecutionFinished` creates an uncertain side-effect record.\n+- Resume never automatically reruns an uncertain mutating tool.\n+- The next turn receives a recovery notice and must inspect state before proceeding.\n+\n+### Turn commit rules\n+\n+- A committed outer turn starts with one accepted user message.\n+- It may contain multiple accepted assistant/tool cycles.\n+- It ends with a terminal accepted assistant step or an explicit durable interruption outcome.\n+- Only committed outer turns are eligible for normal compaction.\n+- An in-flight turn is never split across a compaction boundary.\n+\n+### JSONL recovery\n+\n+- Parse the longest valid prefix of the file.\n+- A malformed final line is quarantined and reported; it does not hide earlier events.\n+- A malformed non-final record is a visible integrity error.\n+- Sequence gaps and duplicate IDs are integrity errors.\n+- Event appends use restrictive permissions, append, flush, and fsync.\n+- Derived indexes may be rebuilt from events without changing event IDs.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 6. Canonical Messages and Provider Continuation\n+\n+### Portable message model\n+\n+```rust\n+enum ConversationMessage {\n+    User(UserMessage),\n+    Assistant(AssistantMessage),\n+    ToolResult(ToolResultMessage),\n+    HistoricalHandoff(HistoricalHandoff),\n+}\n+\n+struct AssistantMessage {\n+    message_id: Ulid,\n+    turn_id: Ulid,\n+    step_id: Ulid,\n+    provider: String,\n+    model: String,\n+    blocks: Vec<AssistantBlock>,\n+    finish_reason: FinishReason,\n+    continuation: Option<ProviderContinuation>,\n+}\n+\n+enum AssistantBlock {\n+    Text(String),\n+    ReasoningSummary(String),\n+    ToolCall(ToolCall),\n+    Image(ImageBlock),\n+}\n+```\n+\n+Block order is preserved. Providers must not reconstruct ordered native output from separate flattened `text`, `thinking`, and `toolCalls` fields.\n+\n+### Provider-native continuation\n+\n+```rust\n+enum ProviderContinuation {\n+    OpenAiResponses(OpenAiResponsesContinuation),\n+    Anthropic(AnthropicContinuation),\n+    Gemini(GeminiContinuation),\n+    Bedrock(BedrockContinuation),\n+}\n+```\n+\n+Each adapter must implement the equivalent of:\n+\n+```rust\n+trait ProviderAdapter {\n+    fn protocol_id(&self) -> &'static str;\n+    fn format_request(&self, request: CanonicalRequest) -> Result<WireRequest>;\n+    fn parse_stream(&self, stream: ByteStream) -> ProviderEventStream;\n+    fn continuation_compatible(&self, state: &ProviderContinuation, model: &str) -> bool;\n+    fn estimate_request_tokens(&self, request: &CanonicalRequest) -> TokenEstimate;\n+}\n+```\n+\n+### Initial reasoning policy\n+\n+```toml\n+[history]\n+reasoning_replay = \"active\"\n+```\n+\n+- Preserve exact native continuation data for the active tool cycle.\n+- Persist it before executing requested tools.\n+- Replay it only to a compatible provider, API, and model family.\n+- Do not index opaque or encrypted reasoning in transcript search.\n+- Do not include old opaque reasoning in compacted context.\n+- Keep conclusions, rationale, uncertainty, and next actions through StateGraph and handoff summaries.\n+- Treat provider-managed IDs such as `previous_response_id` as optional optimizations, never the local source of truth.\n+\n+### Model switching\n+\n+- A model/provider switch creates an explicit protocol boundary.\n+- Drop incompatible opaque continuation state from the active request.\n+- Append a visible handoff describing the prior provider and currently available tool set.\n+- Re-run context admission against the target model's window and output reserve.\n+- Expect and measure a provider/model-specific cache miss.\n+- Do not add automatic per-turn routing in the initial Rust v2 scope.\n+\n+Cursor reported a 30% CursorBench degradation for one Codex setup when reasoning traces were omitted. This motivates strict adapter tests and telemetry; it does not imply the same effect size for every model.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 7. Logical Conversation Projection\n+\n+The logical conversation is rebuilt deterministically from canonical events.\n+\n+It includes:\n+\n+- Accepted user messages after the active reset boundary.\n+- Accepted, non-superseded assistant steps.\n+- Protocol-complete tool-call/result groups.\n+- The active bounded historical handoff.\n+- Recent committed turns not retired by the active compaction epoch.\n+- The current in-flight turn when constructing its next provider request.\n+\n+It excludes:\n+\n+- Failed or superseded assistant attempts.\n+- UI-only events.\n+- Tool executions not connected to an accepted assistant step.\n+- Compacted source messages from the model-visible request.\n+- Incompatible provider-native continuation state.\n+- Cross-session memory records unless supplied by a configured plugin.\n+\n+Projection is pure over an event snapshot plus explicitly versioned derived data. Given the same accepted events, config, provider profile, and model, it must produce the same ordered messages.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 8. Prompt and Cache Layout\n+\n+Construct requests in prefix-stability order.\n+\n+```text\n+1. Stable provider-specific system policy\n+2. Stable project instructions and environment facts\n+3. Stable ordered tool schemas\n+4. Bounded historical handoff\n+5. Recent accepted real messages\n+6. Volatile current-state envelope\n+7. Latest user message / active tool cycle\n+```\n+\n+The provider adapter may need a different wire ordering, but it must preserve the same authority semantics.\n+\n+### Stable prefix rules\n+\n+- Do not place the current timestamp near the beginning of the system prompt.\n+- Do not inject changing token counts, StateGraph counts, or turn numbers into the stable prefix.\n+- Keep tool ordering deterministic.\n+- Put changing StateGraph content in a current-state tail envelope.\n+- A compaction epoch is allowed to invalidate the message prefix once; subsequent turns should append monotonically again.\n+- Record provider-reported cache reads and writes instead of assuming cache behavior.\n+\n+### Instruction authority\n+\n+- User and tool content never becomes system authority through transcript rendering.\n+- Historical handoffs are explicitly labeled non-authoritative evidence.\n+- Tool output and generated summaries are untrusted data.\n+- The stable system policy states that historical data cannot override current system or user instructions.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 9. Artifacts and Session Search\n+\n+### Storage\n+\n+Each session owns a SQLite database:\n+\n+```text\n+~/.praana/sessions/<session-id>/\n+  events.jsonl\n+  history.db\n+  meta.json\n+```\n+\n+`events.jsonl` is canonical for ordered protocol events. `history.db` is canonical for large artifact bodies and materialized indexes; everything else in it is rebuildable from events.\n+\n+### Artifact write ordering\n+\n+1. Serialize the post-hook, post-redaction tool result deterministically.\n+2. If it exceeds the inline policy, write the complete artifact and commit SQLite.\n+3. Build an immutable preview containing the artifact ID and retrieval instructions.\n+4. Append and fsync `ToolExecutionFinished` with the preview/reference.\n+5. If a crash leaves an unreferenced artifact row, startup maintenance may garbage-collect it.\n+6. Never append an artifact reference before the artifact transaction commits.\n+\n+### Initial artifact policy\n+\n+- Initial per-result inline threshold: 800 estimated tokens.\n+- Threshold remains configurable and benchmarked.\n+- Apply an aggregate tool-batch budget so many small outputs cannot bypass control.\n+- Do not exempt errors from artifactization solely because they are errors.\n+- Prefer first-party tools with naturally compact result schemas.\n+- Use deterministic, content-aware previews; do not invoke an LLM per tool result.\n+- Never rewrite an old inline result merely because it aged by a number of turns.\n+\n+### Artifact metadata\n+\n+Store at least:\n+\n+- Artifact ID and SHA-256.\n+- Producing event, turn, attempt, and tool-call IDs.\n+- Tool name and normalized command/path label.\n+- Content type.\n+- Byte, line, and estimated-token counts.\n+- Exit status and stdout/stderr boundaries when applicable.\n+- Source line range for file reads.\n+- Redaction status.\n+- Created/access timestamps and counts.\n+- Immutable preview text.\n+\n+### Retrieval\n+\n+The core `retrieve_artifact` tool supports:\n+\n+- Full retrieval when bounded.\n+- Line range.\n+- Head and tail.\n+- Regex filtering with context.\n+- JSON path or equivalent structured extraction.\n+- Clear errors for missing or out-of-range data.\n+\n+Repeated identical retrieval may return a compact reference after a prior successful retrieval, but must never pretend omitted content was returned.\n+\n+### Search\n+\n+Initial session search combines:\n+\n+- Exact text and regex.\n+- SQLite FTS5/BM25.\n+- Filters for event kind, turn range, tool, path, artifact, and summary segment.\n+- Stable source event IDs and artifact IDs.\n+- Excerpts with exact retrieval instructions.\n+\n+Index accepted visible transcript text and complete redacted artifact bodies. Do not index encrypted provider reasoning.\n+\n+Semantic transcript search is deferred until exact/FTS retrieval is measured and shown insufficient. Codebase semantic search remains a separate capability and is not evidence that transcript embeddings are required.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 10. StateGraph as Current Scratch State\n+\n+StateGraph remains core and mode-independent.\n+\n+```text\n+Canonical events = source of truth\n+StateGraph       = reconstructible current-state projection\n+Summary segments = immutable historical narrative/evidence\n+Current handoff  = bounded context carried across compaction\n+```\n+\n+StateGraph owns current:\n+\n+- Tasks and status.\n+- Decisions and rationale.\n+- Constraints.\n+- Notes/findings.\n+- Open errors.\n+- Focus and next actions.\n+\n+### Rules\n+\n+- Every mutation appends a `StateChanged` event.\n+- Updates supersede stale current state rather than appending contradictory prompt prose.\n+- Active entries appear in the volatile request tail.\n+- Soft/hard entries are available through state/search tools.\n+- Checkpoints accelerate resume but are verified against an event sequence/hash.\n+- StateGraph can be rebuilt from events if a checkpoint is missing or invalid.\n+- Automatic tiering remains experimental and observable.\n+- Engine mode may use StateGraph for scoring, but append mode does not run per-turn historical scoring.\n+\n+This preserves the useful scratchpad/checkpoint part of the current engine without requiring its per-turn BM25/semantic curation pipeline.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 11. Request Admission and Context Pressure\n+\n+The 60% threshold starts compaction; it does not guarantee a request fits.\n+\n+Before every provider request, including every tool-loop continuation and fallback retry, calculate:\n+\n+```text\n+stable system and project context\n++ tool schemas\n++ current handoff\n++ retained accepted messages\n++ StateGraph tail\n++ active tool protocol state\n++ provider framing estimate\n++ requested output/reasoning reserve\n++ estimator safety margin\n+```\n+\n+### Admission policy\n+\n+- Resolve the actual provider/model context window first.\n+- Include tool schemas and provider framing.\n+- Use a real model tokenizer where reliable; otherwise use a conservative estimator.\n+- Use provider usage as post-request calibration, not sole preflight protection.\n+- Reserve actual configured output/reasoning allowance rather than defaulting to zero.\n+- Re-admit after model/provider/reasoning-effort changes.\n+- Re-admit after every tool batch.\n+- Record estimated versus provider-reported occupancy.\n+\n+### Initial thresholds\n+\n+```toml\n+[history]\n+mode = \"append\"\n+compact_at = 0.60\n+compact_clear_at = 0.45\n+compact_mass_fraction = 0.50\n+reasoning_replay = \"active\"\n+artifact_inline_tokens = 800\n+```\n+\n+`compact_mass_fraction` applies only to eligible committed historical messages. System policy, tool schemas, current StateGraph, the active user request, and incomplete tool protocol groups are never counted as retireable mass.\n+\n+### Hard-ceiling behavior\n+\n+1. Artifactize every eligible large result in the active request representation.\n+2. Compact additional oldest committed turns.\n+3. Reduce requested output allowance only within a provider-safe configured minimum.\n+4. If the active turn alone cannot fit, stop cleanly with a continuation instruction.\n+5. On a provider context-length error, perform at most one emergency admission/compaction retry.\n+6. Never loop indefinitely on context errors.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 12. Compaction\n+\n+### Trigger and selection\n+\n+- Prefer compaction between outer turns.\n+- Permit mid-turn compaction only over previously committed turns; preserve the full active tool cycle.\n+- Trigger at projected 60% usable fill.\n+- Select oldest complete committed turns until approximately 50% of eligible historical token mass is retired.\n+- Re-estimate after compaction and retire more complete turns if the request still exceeds the hard ceiling.\n+- Do not preserve an arbitrary fixed number of recent turns if they do not fit.\n+\n+### Capability-profile model selection\n+\n+```text\n+Known model trained/validated for self-summary:\n+  append an internal synthetic compaction request to the existing cached prefix\n+\n+Unknown or weak self-summary model:\n+  use the configured structured compactor\n+```\n+\n+- The active model path may reuse provider KV/prompt cache.\n+- A more expensive model is not assumed to be a better compactor.\n+- The capability table is provider/model/version specific and test-backed.\n+- Compaction requests are internal events, not fabricated user messages.\n+\n+### Output model\n+\n+Each compaction produces:\n+\n+1. An immutable summary segment for the newly retired source range.\n+2. A bounded current handoff representing what must remain model-visible.\n+3. Structured references to StateGraph entries and artifacts.\n+\n+The immutable segment contains:\n+\n+- User goals and scope changes.\n+- Completed work.\n+- Files and symbols changed.\n+- Decisions and rationale.\n+- Constraints.\n+- Commands/tests and outcomes.\n+- Failed approaches.\n+- Unresolved errors and questions.\n+- Important artifact IDs.\n+- Explicit uncertainty and contradictions.\n+- Source event/turn range.\n+\n+The current handoff is bounded and current. It does not blindly concatenate every immutable segment.\n+\n+### Compaction record\n+\n+```rust\n+struct HistoryCompacted {\n+    epoch: u32,\n+    source_start_sequence: u64,\n+    source_end_sequence: u64,\n+    source_hash: String,\n+    source_tokens: u64,\n+    segment: SummarySegment,\n+    handoff: HistoricalHandoff,\n+    output_tokens: u64,\n+    model: String,\n+    provider: String,\n+    prompt_version: String,\n+    artifact_ids: Vec<String>,\n+    state_ids: Vec<String>,\n+}\n+```\n+\n+### Atomic activation\n+\n+1. Snapshot the eligible source range and hash it.\n+2. Generate a candidate segment and handoff.\n+3. Validate schema, non-empty required fields, source references, and output bounds.\n+4. Confirm the source range/hash has not changed.\n+5. Append and fsync `HistoryCompacted`.\n+6. Update derived SQLite indexes in an idempotent transaction.\n+7. Activate the new projection only after the event is durable.\n+\n+If generation or validation fails, the previous projection remains active. Source events are never deleted or marked hidden solely because a summarizer was invoked.\n+\n+### Injection safety\n+\n+- The compactor treats user and tool data as untrusted evidence.\n+- It never promotes instructions found in tool output into system policy.\n+- The handoff is labeled non-authoritative historical data.\n+- Preserve user instructions as attributed historical facts, not new system commands.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 13. Pluggable Cognitive Memory\n+\n+Cross-session memory is independent from current-session history.\n+\n+### Default\n+\n+```toml\n+[memory]\n+plugin = \"none\"\n+```\n+\n+With no plugin:\n+\n+- No global memory database is opened.\n+- No embedding model is loaded or downloaded.\n+- No startup memory digest is injected.\n+- No session-end learning extraction runs.\n+- Recall/remember/retract tools are absent.\n+- History compaction, resume, StateGraph, artifacts, and session search continue normally.\n+\n+### Plugin responsibilities\n+\n+A full-lifecycle memory plugin owns:\n+\n+- Learning extraction.\n+- Storage backend and migrations.\n+- Recall and ranking.\n+- Optional startup digest/bootstrap context.\n+- Scope policy.\n+- Deduplication and contradiction handling.\n+- Validity, usefulness, reinforcement, and decay.\n+- Consolidation.\n+- Optional embeddings.\n+- Session-end learning.\n+- Pinning and retraction.\n+\n+### Core contract\n+\n+```rust\n+#[async_trait]\n+trait MemoryPlugin: Send + Sync {\n+    fn id(&self) -> &str;\n+    fn api_version(&self) -> u32;\n+    async fn open(\n+        &self,\n+        host: Arc<dyn MemoryPluginHost>,\n+        options: serde_json::Value,\n+    ) -> Result<Box<dyn MemorySession>>;\n+}\n+\n+#[async_trait]\n+trait MemorySession: Send {\n+    fn capabilities(&self) -> MemoryCapabilities;\n+    async fn start(&mut self, context: MemorySessionContext) -> Result<MemoryBootstrap>;\n+    async fn recall(&mut self, query: RecallQuery) -> Result<RecallResult>;\n+    async fn remember(&mut self, input: RememberInput) -> Result<RememberResult>;\n+    async fn retract(&mut self, id: &str) -> Result<()>;\n+    async fn end(&mut self, input: MemorySessionEnd) -> Result<MemorySessionEndResult>;\n+    async fn stats(&self) -> Result<MemoryStats>;\n+    async fn close(self: Box<Self>) -> Result<()>;\n+}\n+```\n+\n+The host exposes narrow logging, clock, cancellation, and LLM-completion capabilities. It does not expose the whole session, provider credentials, arbitrary tools, or filesystem access.\n+\n+### Data boundary\n+\n+Plugins may receive:\n+\n+- Accepted visible transcript.\n+- Current StateGraph snapshot.\n+- Project/user/agent scope identifiers.\n+- Redacted artifact summaries and references.\n+- Session outcome signals.\n+- Explicit `remember` inputs.\n+\n+Plugins do not receive:\n+\n+- Superseded attempts.\n+- Opaque/encrypted provider reasoning.\n+- Provider credentials.\n+- Raw unredacted artifacts.\n+- Tool execution handles.\n+- The full core `Session` object.\n+\n+### Tool ownership\n+\n+Core defines stable `recall`, `remember`, and `retract_memory` tool schemas. It registers them only when the plugin advertises the corresponding capability. Plugins do not inject arbitrary tool definitions in v1.\n+\n+### First-party implementation\n+\n+- Implement `builtin:sqlite` after the contract tests exist.\n+- Keep it disabled unless explicitly configured.\n+- Start with exact/FTS/BM25 recall and no embeddings.\n+- Keep its schema and lifecycle entirely plugin-owned.\n+- Allow a later optional semantic feature without making ONNX part of the default binary.\n+\n+### External plugins\n+\n+External dynamic loading is deferred until the contract stabilizes.\n+\n+- Do not use Rust dylibs as the primary plugin API; Rust has no stable ABI.\n+- Prefer a versioned subprocess JSONL/JSON-RPC protocol for language independence and crash isolation.\n+- Consider WASI Components later if sandboxing and portable plugin artifacts justify the runtime cost.\n+\n+### Existing couplings to remove\n+\n+- `Session` no longer exposes a concrete `MemoryStore`.\n+- Engine scoring cannot borrow `memoryStore.embedder`.\n+- Skill usefulness moves to core telemetry/session storage.\n+- Scorecard cannot read a concrete memory database path.\n+- Artifact promotion becomes optional plugin session-end behavior.\n+- Core history compaction does not call the memory plugin.\n+\n+Memory failure is always soft. A missing, failed, or timed-out plugin never prevents a turn, resume, compaction, or shutdown.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 14. Safety and Tool Pipeline\n+\n+Preserve the current logical order:\n+\n+```text\n+pre-tool:\n+  plan mode -> validation -> risk -> circuit -> write-path acquire\n+\n+execute tool\n+\n+post-tool:\n+  LSP -> verify -> enrich -> redact -> circuit accounting -> write-path release\n+```\n+\n+### Rust requirements\n+\n+- Tool schemas are generated from typed request structures and are deterministic.\n+- Validation happens before risk confirmation or lock acquisition.\n+- Write-path locks are released on success, error, cancellation, and panic boundaries.\n+- Mutating tools preserve circuit-breaker behavior.\n+- Redaction occurs before persistent artifacts and model-visible results are finalized.\n+- User and agent transcript privacy policy is explicit and separate from tool-result redaction.\n+- Shell timeouts terminate process groups on Unix and Job Objects on Windows.\n+- Cancellation is structured with one session/turn token, not ad hoc booleans.\n+- Panics do not cross plugin, provider, tool, or IPC boundaries.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 15. Initial Provider Scope\n+\n+### OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions\n+\n+Support:\n+\n+- OpenAI and OpenRouter endpoint configuration.\n+- Standard and custom headers.\n+- Streaming usage when available.\n+- Parallel fragmented tool calls.\n+- Provider compatibility flags.\n+- Reasoning text fields used by OpenRouter-compatible models.\n+- Deterministic request fixtures.\n+\n+### OpenAI Responses\n+\n+Support:\n+\n+- Ordered response output items.\n+- Function calls and outputs.\n+- Reasoning items and encrypted reasoning items.\n+- Response/continuation identifiers when available.\n+- Tool-call argument fragmentation.\n+- Usage and cache accounting.\n+- Same-model continuation across tool calls.\n+- Explicit reset behavior after compaction or model switch.\n+\n+### Retry policy\n+\n+- Retry only before accepted output/tool-call emission unless the adapter explicitly supports idempotent continuation.\n+- Each retry is a new attempt in canonical history.\n+- Never execute tool calls from a failed partial provider attempt.\n+- Respect rate-limit retry hints within a bounded policy.\n+- Context-length failure receives at most one emergency admission retry.\n+\n+Anthropic, Gemini/Vertex, Bedrock, Azure, OAuth variations, and custom provider edge cases are later parity phases.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 16. Temporary TypeScript UI Bridge\n+\n+Do not expand N-API to host the stateful Rust turn engine. Use a long-lived child process with framed JSONL messages.\n+\n+### Commands from UI to core\n+\n+- Create/resume/end session.\n+- Submit user input.\n+- Abort turn.\n+- Confirm/deny risk action.\n+- Run slash command.\n+- Change model/reasoning/settings.\n+- Request transcript page or expanded artifact.\n+\n+### Events from core to UI\n+\n+- Session metadata and boot status.\n+- Assistant text/thinking deltas.\n+- Attempt started/rewound/accepted.\n+- Tool call/result state.\n+- Usage and cache updates.\n+- System notices and errors.\n+- Risk confirmation requests.\n+- Turn completion/interruption.\n+- Transcript paging data.\n+\n+### IPC rules\n+\n+- Versioned handshake before session commands.\n+- Monotonic event sequence per connection.\n+- Request IDs for commands requiring responses.\n+- Bounded frames and explicit large-payload artifact references.\n+- Backpressure and cancellation behavior.\n+- Child crash is surfaced visibly; the UI may restart and resume from durable session state.\n+- IPC DTOs are language-neutral and reusable by future external memory plugins where appropriate.\n+\n+The TypeScript UI remains a client only. New session/context behavior belongs in Rust.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 17. Ratatui Cutover\n+\n+Ratatui work starts only after the Rust core passes headless, persistence, compaction, and provider gates.\n+\n+Feature parity includes:\n+\n+- Streaming transcript and thinking display.\n+- Virtualized/paged historical transcript.\n+- Expandable artifact/tool rows.\n+- Multiline input and paste handling.\n+- Slash command palette.\n+- Model selector.\n+- Setup/login/logout/consent flows.\n+- Scrolling, tail follow, focus, and overlays.\n+- Markdown and syntax highlighting.\n+- Debug/status/usage views.\n+- Accessible terminal fallback behavior.\n+\n+Use terminal snapshot tests and PTY integration tests. Treat differences as explicit UX decisions, not accidental omissions.\n+\n+After parity:\n+\n+- Remove OpenTUI, Solid, Bun preload/build code, and TypeScript UI.\n+- Remove the N-API crate and `.node` release sidecar.\n+- Keep only standalone native release artifacts and install scripts for the first Rust-native release.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 18. Observability and Evaluation\n+\n+Every run records enough dimensions to distinguish language, provider, and context-policy changes.\n+\n+```text\n+implementation = ts | rust\n+history_mode = append | engine\n+event_schema_version\n+projection_version\n+compaction_policy_version\n+provider_driver_version\n+model\n+memory_plugin_id/version\n+artifact_policy_version\n+```\n+\n+### Context metrics\n+\n+- Estimated and provider-reported input occupancy.\n+- Output/reasoning reserve.\n+- Cached and uncached input tokens.\n+- Cache invalidation at compaction/model switch.\n+- Number, source size, output size, and latency of compactions.\n+- Summary compression ratio.\n+- Artifact cards produced and retrieved.\n+- Search calls, hits, and evidence used.\n+- Repeat reads/tool calls and churn.\n+\n+### Correctness metrics\n+\n+- End-task tests and task-specific graders.\n+- User goal and constraint retention after compaction.\n+- Open-task/error recall.\n+- Unsupported summary statements.\n+- Contradictions and stale facts.\n+- Exact source citation/retrieval success.\n+- Lost subgoals and duplicated work.\n+- Invalid provider protocol requests.\n+- Reasoning continuation retained/dropped.\n+- Resume correctness after injected crashes.\n+\n+### Initial ablations\n+\n+1. Reasoning continuation enabled versus deliberately removed.\n+2. Inline versus artifactized large outputs.\n+3. Exact/FTS history search available versus unavailable.\n+4. StateGraph tail available versus unavailable.\n+5. Structured compactor versus capability-profile self-summary.\n+6. Rust append mode versus the TypeScript engine baseline, with implementation recorded as a confounder.\n+\n+### Threshold sweeps\n+\n+After the default path is stable, evaluate:\n+\n+- Trigger ratios: 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, 80%.\n+- Eligible mass retirement: 25%, 50%, 75%.\n+- Artifact inline thresholds and aggregate batch budgets.\n+- Handoff output budgets.\n+- Same-model versus configured-compactor behavior by model family.\n+\n+Do not optimize tool-call count, commit count, or generated lines as primary quality measures. Cursor's swarm research showed that high activity can represent churn rather than progress.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 19. Verification Strategy\n+\n+### TypeScript oracle\n+\n+Keep the current implementation runnable during migration.\n+\n+- Capture black-box fixtures before replacing stable behavior.\n+- Compare only contracts marked \"preserve\"; do not require parity for intentionally replaced compilers or memory behavior.\n+- Record exact config/environment/clock/ID seeds in fixtures.\n+- Keep TypeScript tests until the corresponding Rust behavior has independent coverage.\n+\n+### Golden provider fixtures\n+\n+For each supported protocol, cover:\n+\n+- Exact request JSON and headers.\n+- UTF-8 and SSE boundaries split at every relevant location.\n+- CRLF/LF framing.\n+- Multiple concurrent tool calls.\n+- Fragmented tool arguments.\n+- Usage-only events.\n+- Disconnect before and after accepted emission.\n+- Rate limits, timeouts, and aborts.\n+- Reasoning/encrypted continuation items.\n+- Context-length errors and emergency retry.\n+- Resume of a complete active tool cycle.\n+\n+### Persistence fault injection\n+\n+Crash after each durable boundary:\n+\n+- User accepted.\n+- Assistant attempt started.\n+- Assistant step accepted.\n+- Tool execution started.\n+- Artifact committed.\n+- Tool execution finished.\n+- Tool batch completed.\n+- Turn committed.\n+- Compaction event appended.\n+- Derived index update.\n+\n+Verify that resume never invents completion, loses prior valid records, or reruns uncertain side effects.\n+\n+### Property/fuzz tests\n+\n+Use property testing and fuzzing for:\n+\n+- SSE parsing.\n+- Tool-call accumulation.\n+- JSONL recovery.\n+- Event projection.\n+- Tool protocol pairing.\n+- Compaction boundaries and source hashes.\n+- Artifact line/range filters.\n+- FTS source mapping.\n+- Path sandbox normalization.\n+- Secret redaction.\n+- IPC framing.\n+- Future plugin framing.\n+\n+Core invariants:\n+\n+- Canonical events are never rewritten.\n+- Every visible tool result references a visible tool call.\n+- Every committed turn is protocol-complete.\n+- Every artifact reference resolves before its event becomes visible.\n+- Compaction never deletes source evidence.\n+- StateGraph can be rebuilt from canonical events.\n+- A plugin failure cannot break session history.\n+- No redacted tool secret appears in a persisted artifact or model-visible result.\n+\n+### Rust quality gates\n+\n+```bash\n+cargo fmt --all -- --check\n+cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings\n+cargo test --workspace\n+```\n+\n+Add target-specific smoke tests for Linux x64/arm64, macOS arm64/x64, and logic, and a Rust child crash resumes from durable state with a visible notice.\n+\n+### Phase 8: Provider and tool parity\n+\n+- [ ] Port Anthropic with thinking signatures.\n+- [ ] Port Rust engine projection plan over the same canonical events/artifacts.\n+- [ ] Otherwise archive the engine as research evidence and remove the mode from the final config.\n+\n+**Exit criteria:** The engine is either implemented as a non-mutating alternative projection or explicitly retired based on measured evidence.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 21. Risks and Mitigations\n+\n+| Risk | Mitigation |\n+|---|---|\n+| AI produces plausible but wrong provider serializers | Golden request/stream fixtures, reasoning-item assertions, provider-specific integration tests |\n+| Three changes are confused: language, history policy, memory | Record implementation, projection, compaction, and plugin versions in every eval |\n+| Rust rewrite stalls product work | Keep each phase independently runnable; headless MVP before TUI/provider parity |\n+| OpenTUI rewrite consumes the project | Keep TypeScript as a temporary IPC client; Ratatui is a separate late phase |\n+| Compaction drops critical details | Immutable source evidence, bounded current handoff, StateGraph, searchable artifacts, fidelity probes |\n+| Summary segments accumulate | Store all segments but expose one bounded current handoff |\n+| Provider reasoning is lost | First-class continuation enum, active-cycle persistence, adapter capability tests and telemetry |\n+| Append-only log contains failed attempts | Logical accepted projection plus explicit supersession |\n+| Crash leaves uncertain side effects | Tool-start/finish durability and inspect-before-continue recovery notices |\n+| Artifact reference points to missing data | Commit artifact before event; startup integrity checks |\n+| SQLite becomes a new global coupling | Per-session core DB; plugin-owned cross-session storage |\n+| Memory plugin crashes core | Narrow trait/host boundary, timeouts, soft failure; external plugins later use processes/WASM |\n+| Plugins leak sensitive data | Sanitized accepted transcript only; no credentials or opaque reasoning; explicit permissions later |\n+| Binary size/build time explodes | No default ONNX/AWS/WASM stack; add provider/plugin features incrementally |\n+| Cache savings are assumed rather than observed | Record cache read/write tokens, TTFT, and compaction/model-switch invalidations |\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 24. Definition of Done\n+\n+Rust v2 is complete when:\n+\n+- `praana` is a standalone Rust binary with no Bun runtime requirement.\n+- Canonical events durably represent real provider messages, attempts, tools, compaction, and StateGraph changes.\n+- Resume handles committed turns, active complete tool cycles, failed attempts, truncated final records, and uncertain tools safely.\n+- OpenAI/OpenRouter plus all providers intentionally retained for release pass fixture and smoke tests.\n+- Provider-native reasoning continuation is preserved where supported and explicitly reset where incompatible.\n+- Append history is the default and classic history no longer exists.\n+- Large tool output is lossless, stored once, searchable, and recoverable by artifact ID.\n+- Compaction uses complete committed turns, immutable summary evidence, a bounded current handoff, and atomic activation.\n+- Request admission runs before every provider call and reserves output/reasoning space.\n+- StateGraph is an event-derived current-state projection available in the default mode.\n+- Cross-session memory is disabled by default and available only through the full-lifecycle plugin contract.\n+- No embedding model or cross-session memory database is required by the default installation.\n+- Core, persistence, provider, fault-injection, security, PTY, and release-matrix tests pass.\n+- The TypeScript runtime, OpenTUI client, N-API wrapper, and native sidecar are removed after Ratatui parity.\n+- The engine comparison has a measured implement-or-retire decision.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 25. Research Basis and Limits\n+\n+Relevant Cursor publications informed this plan:\n+\n+- [Dynamic context discovery](https://cursor.com/blog/dynamic-context-discovery): lossless searchable large outputs and searchable chat after summarization.\n+- [Training Composer for longer horizons](https://cursor.com/blog/self-summarization): repeated compaction, retained plan/task state, model-trained self-summary, and cache reuse.\n+- [Improving Cursor's agent for OpenAI Codex models](https://cursor.com/blog/codex-model-harness): provider reasoning-trace continuity and model-specific harness behavior.\n+- [Continually improving our agent harness](https://cursor.com/blog/continually-improving-agent-harness): dynamic rather than large static context, model-switch costs, context rot, and online/offline measurement.\n+- [What we've learned building cloud agents](https://cursor.com/blog/cloud-agent-lessons): append-only conversation storage, retries/supersession, durable execution, and separation of conversation from runtime state.\n+- [Towards self-driving codebases](https://cursor.com/blog/self-driving-codebases): fresh mutable scratch state, automatic summarization, structured handoffs, and observability.\n+- [Fast regex search](https://cursor.com/blog/fast-regex-search) and [Improving agent with semantic search](https://cursor.com/blog/semsearch): exact search freshness and the complementary role of semantic code search.\n+- [How we compare model quality in Cursor](https://cursor.com/blog/cursorbench): realistic long-task evaluation across correctness, efficiency, and interaction quality.\n+\n+These publications validate the direction, not PRAANA's exact constants. In particular, they do not establish 60%, 50%, 800 tokens, immutable segments, or any one summary budget as universally optimal. Those values remain hypotheses to test.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## 26. 52: 
53: ## 2. Why Rust v2 Is a Redesign, Not a Port
54: 
55: The current repository contains approximately 54K lines of TypeScript source, 41K lines of TypeScript tests, 9K lines of UI/TUI code, and 2K lines of Rust native code. A line-by-line rewrite would preserve obsolete architecture and create a large semantic verification burden.
56: 
57: Rust v2 must instead preserve contracts that still matter and deliberately replace the rest.
58: 
59: ### Preserve
60: 
61: - Provider wire correctness, including streaming and tool calls.
62: - Safety-hook behavior and ordering.
63: - Shell process-tree cancellation.
64: - Credential and secret-handling expectations.
65: - Config source precedence where retained by the v2 config spec.
66: - StateGraph semantics that remain useful.
67: - Lossless source artifacts and filtered retrieval.
68: - Headless operation and Harbor compatibility.
69: - Interactive behavior while the TypeScript UI remains the client.
70: 
71: ### Replace
72: 
73: - Per-turn reconstruction of cross-turn history into a system-prompt string.
74: - The current reduced event log as the only resume substrate.
75: - The coupling between Cognitive Memory, embeddings, skills, artifacts, scorecard, and the context engine.
76: - The compression checkpoint sidecar as authoritative state.
77: - The concrete `MemoryStore` dependency throughout `Session` and tools.
78: - Duplicate transcript representations that can disagree.
79: 
80: ### Delete rather than port
81: 
82: - `src/compile-classic.ts`.
83: - `src/auto-compact.ts` behavior that writes old turns into Cognitive Memory.
84: - Classic-mode branching and naming.
85: - Old session/database migrations.
86: - Default ONNX embedding setup.
87: - N-API packaging after the TypeScript client is retired.
88: - Bun-specific global package installation as an initial v2 requirement.
89: 
90: AI-assisted implementation reduces typing and translation cost. It does not reduce the need for wire fixtures, crash tests, security checks, or semantic comparison. Compilation is necessary but never sufficient acceptance evidence.
91: 
92: ---
93: 
94: ## 3. Target Runtime Architecture
95: 
96: ```text
97: User / headless caller / temporary TypeScript UI
98:                     |
99:                     v
100:               Rust application
101:                     |
102:           +---------+---------+
103:           |                   |
104:           v                   v
105:    Session controller      UI event sink
106:           |
107:           v
108:    Turn orchestrator
109:           |
110:           +--> request admission
111:           +--> provider adapter
112:           +--> tool/safety pipeline
113:           +--> canonical event append
114:           +--> logical history projection
115:           +--> artifact/session search
116:           +--> StateGraph projection
117:           +--> compaction projection
118:           +--> optional memory plugin
119: ```
120: 
121: The core separates storage from what the model sees.
122: 
123: ```text
124: Canonical event history
125:   Every accepted or failed attempt, tool execution, state change,
126:   compaction, reset, model switch, and supersession
127:                     |
128:                     v
129: Logical accepted conversation
130:   Only accepted user/assistant messages and protocol-complete tool groups
131:                     |
132:                     v
133: Model-visible request
134:   Stable system/tool prefix + bounded handoff + current StateGraph
135:   + recent accepted real messages + current in-flight tool cycle
136: ```
137: 
138: Append-only describes the durable record. It does not require feeding failed, superseded, compacted, or protocol-incompatible records to the model.

937: ## 18. Observability and Evaluation
938: 
939: Every run records enough dimensions to distinguish language, provider, and context-policy changes.
940: 
941: ```text
942: implementation = ts | rust
943: history_mode = append | engine
944: event_schema_version
945: projection_version
946: compaction_policy_version
947: provider_driver_version
948: model
949: memory_plugin_id/version
950: artifact_policy_version
951: ```
952: 
953: ### Context metrics
954: 
955: - Estimated and provider-reported input occupancy.
956: - Output/reasoning reserve.
957: - Cached and uncached input tokens.
958: - Cache invalidation at compaction/model switch.
959: - Number, source size, output size, and latency of compactions.
960: - Summary compression ratio.
961: - Artifact cards produced and retrieved.
962: - Search calls, hits, and evidence used.
963: - Repeat reads/tool calls and churn.
964: 
965: ### Correctness metrics
966: 
967: - End-task tests and task-specific graders.
968: - User goal and constraint retention after compaction.
969: - Open-task/error recall.
970: - Unsupported summary statements.
971: - Contradictions and stale facts.
972: - Exact source citation/retrieval success.
973: - Lost subgoals and duplicated work.
974: - Invalid provider protocol requests.
975: - Reasoning continuation retained/dropped.
976: - Resume correctness after injected crashes.
977: 
978: ### Initial ablations
979: 
980: 1. Reasoning continuation enabled versus deliberately removed.
981: 2. Inline versus artifactized large outputs.
982: 3. Exact/FTS history search available versus unavailable.
983: 4. StateGraph tail available versus unavailable.
984: 5. Structured compactor versus capability-profile self-summary.
985: 6. Rust append mode versus the TypeScript engine baseline, with implementation recorded as a confounder.
986: 
987: ### Threshold sweeps
988: 
989: After the default path is stable, evaluate:
990: 
991: - Trigger ratios: 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, 80%.
992: - Eligible mass retirement: 25%, 50%, 75%.
993: - Artifact inline thresholds and aggregate batch budgets.
994: - Handoff output budgets.
995: - Same-model versus configured-compactor behavior by model family.
996: 
997: Do not optimize tool-call count, commit count, or generated lines as primary quality measures. Cursor's swarm research showed that high activity can represent churn rather than progress.

1001: ## 19. Verification Strategy
1002: 
1003: ### TypeScript oracle
1004: 
1005: Keep the current implementation runnable during migration.
1006: 
1007: - Capture black-box fixtures before replacing stable behavior.
1008: - Compare only contracts marked "preserve"; do not require parity for intentionally replaced compilers or memory behavior.
1009: - Record exact config/environment/clock/ID seeds in fixtures.
1010: - Keep TypeScript tests until the corresponding Rust behavior has independent coverage.
1011: 
1012: ### Golden provider fixtures
1013: 
1014: For each supported protocol, cover:
1015: 
1016: - Exact request JSON and headers.
1017: - UTF-8 and SSE boundaries split at every relevant location.
1018: - CRLF/LF framing.
1019: - Multiple concurrent tool calls.
1020: - Fragmented tool arguments.
1021: - Usage-only events.
1022: - Disconnect before and after accepted emission.
1023: - Rate limits, timeouts, and aborts.
1024: - Reasoning/encrypted continuation items.
1025: - Context-length errors and emergency retry.
1026: - Resume of a complete active tool cycle.
1027: 
1028: ### Persistence fault injection
1029: 
1030: Crash after each durable boundary:
1031: 
1032: - User accepted.
1033: - Assistant attempt started.
1034: - Assistant step accepted.
1035: - Tool execution started.
1036: - Artifact committed.
1037: - Tool execution finished.
1038: - Tool batch completed.
1039: - Turn committed.
1040: - Compaction event appended.
1041: - Derived index update.
1042: 
1043: Verify that resume never invents completion, loses prior valid records, or reruns uncertain side effects.
1044: 
1045: ### Property/fuzz tests
1046: 
1047: Use property testing and fuzzing for:
1048: 
1049: - SSE parsing.
1050: - Tool-call accumulation.
1051: - JSONL recovery.
1052: - Event projection.
1053: - Tool protocol pairing.
1054: - Compaction boundaries and source hashes.
1055: - Artifact line/range filters.
1056: - FTS source mapping.
1057: - Path sandbox normalization.
1058: - Secret redaction.
1059: - IPC framing.
1060: - Future plugin framing.
1061: 
1062: Core invariants:
1063: 
1064: - Canonical events are never rewritten.
1065: - Every visible tool result references a visible tool call.
1066: - Every committed turn is protocol-complete.
1067: - Every artifact reference resolves before its event becomes visible.
1068: - Compaction never deletes source evidence.
1069: - StateGraph can be rebuilt from canonical events.
1070: - A plugin failure cannot break session history.
1071: - No redacted tool secret appears in a persisted artifact or model-visible result.
1072:

1074:

1076: cargo fmt --all -- --check
1077: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
1078: cargo test --workspace
1079: ```

**Purpose Of Protocol Spec**

It should remove ambiguity from the most dangerous foundation:

- Canonical events
- Real conversation messages
- Tool-call/result pairing
- Attempts, retries, and supersession
- Turn commit boundaries
- Provider reasoning continuation
- Crash recovery
- Logical conversation projection
- JSONL persistence
- Compaction boundaries

It should contain exact Rust definitions, not only descriptions.

```rust
#[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")]
enum CanonicalEvent {
    SessionStarted(SessionStarted),
    UserMessageAccepted(UserMessageAccepted),
    TurnStarted(TurnStarted),
    AssistantAttemptStarted(AssistantAttemptStarted),
    AssistantAttemptFailed(AssistantAttemptFailed),
    AssistantStepAccepted(AssistantStepAccepted),
    AttemptSuperseded(AttemptSuperseded),
    ToolExecutionStarted(ToolExecutionStarted),
    ToolExecutionFinished(ToolExecutionFinished),
    ToolBatchCompleted(ToolBatchCompleted),
    TurnCommitted(TurnCommitted),
    HistoryCompacted(HistoryCompacted),
}
```

The document should specify:

1. Exact fields and Serde representation for every type.
2. Required IDs and their relationships.
3. Valid and invalid event transitions.
4. Normal text-only turn example.
5. Single tool-call turn example.
6. Parallel tool-call example.
7. Multi-step tool loop example.
8. Provider retry and supersession example.
9. Interrupted tool execution example.
10. Crash at every persistence boundary.
11. Resume projection algorithm.
12. OpenAI Responses reasoning-item representation.
13. Model-switch continuation reset.
14. Reset and compaction boundaries.
15. Golden JSONL fixtures.
16. Exact unit/property tests.
17. Error types and recovery behavior.
18. Explicit non-goals.

**Executable Specifications**

Detailed prose helps, but tests prevent mistakes. Every spec should produce machine-verifiable fixtures:

```text
fixtures/protocol/
  text-turn.jsonl
  single-tool-turn.jsonl
  parallel-tools.jsonl
  multi-step-tools.jsonl
  retry-before-output.jsonl
  superseded-attempt.jsonl
  interrupted-read.jsonl
  uncertain-edit.jsonl
  truncated-final-line.jsonl
  compacted-history.jsonl
  model-switch.jsonl
  openai-reasoning-continuation.jsonl
```

For every fixture, the specification should state:

```text
Expected accepted messages
Expected excluded events
Expected incomplete calls
Expected recovery notices
Expected compaction eligibility
Expected provider continuation state
Expected integrity errors
```

## Document Sequence

After the protocol specification, create these documents in order:

1. `docs/RUST_V2_PHASE_0_EXECUTION.md`
   Exact Cargo changes, crate layout, fixture capture, test helpers, and native-core extraction.

2. `docs/RUST_V2_OPENAI_SPEC.md`

4. `docs/RUST_V2_COMPACTION_SPEC.md`

5. `docs/RUST_V2_STATE_GRAPH_SPEC.md`

6. `docs/RUST_V2_MEMORY_PLUGIN_SPEC.md`

7. `docs/RUST_V2_TOOL_RUNTIME_SPEC.md`

Each specification should then get a small execution packet. The cheaper model should receive only one packet at a time.

## Recommended Implementation Workflow

```text
Strong model:
  Architecture/specification
  Exact interfaces
  Fixtures and invariants
  Review findings

Cheaper model:
  One bounded implementation packet
  Tests first
  No architecture decisions
  No unrelated refactoring

Automated gates:
  fmt
  clippy
  unit tests
  property tests
  golden fixtures
  integration tests

Strong model:
  Final diff review against specification
```

- Exact files to create or modify
- Complete type signatures
- Tests to write first
- Commands to run
- Expected failure before implementation
- Expected output after implementation
- Explicit non-goals
- Common mistakes
- Completion checklist

1: # PRAANA Rust v2 OpenAI and OpenRouter Protocol Specification
2: 
3: Status: Normative v1
4: 
5: Date: 2026-08-31
6: 
7: Scope: OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, and the OpenAI/OpenRouter provider profiles for Rust v2.
8: 
9: ## 1. Normative Language
10: 
11: The terms MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY are normative.
12: 
13: This specification defines new Rust v2 behavior. It does not require compatibility with old PRAANA config, sessions, databases, event schemas, TypeScript message flattening, malformed tool-argument repair, OpenAI key fallback for OpenRouter, or undocumented gateway quirks.
14: 
15: The TypeScript implementation is evidence for behavior explicitly retained here. It is not the authority where this specification makes a different decision.
16: 
17: ## 2. Protocol Scope
18: 
19: Rust v2 initially implements these combinations:
20: 
21: | Provider profile | Protocol ID | Endpoint | Supported |
22: |---|---|---|---|
23: | `openai` | `openai-chat-v1` | `/chat/completions` | Yes |
24: | `openai` | `openai-responses-v1` | `/responses` | Yes |
25: | `openrouter` | `openai-chat-v1` | `/chat/completions` | Yes |
26: | `openrouter` | `openai-responses-v1` | `/responses` | No |
27: 
28: OpenRouter Responses support is out of scope for v1. It MUST NOT be inferred from endpoint availability. Selecting that combination returns `unsupported_protocol` before auth or network access.
29: 
30: The generic Chat serializer is profile-driven, but v1 ships only the two profiles above. Azure, OpenAI Codex OAuth, DeepSeek, Groq, Ollama, custom gateways, Anthropic, Gemini, and Bedrock are separate specifications.
31: 
32: ## 3. Core Invariants
33: 
34: - Canonical accepted messages are the local source of truth.
35: - Provider response IDs are never the local source of truth.
36: - The adapter never executes tools.
37: - The adapter never repairs malformed streamed JSON arguments.
38: - Tool calls from a failed, aborted, truncated, or superseded attempt are never executable.
39: - Parallel calls and results are associated by call ID, not name or completion order.
40: - Provider output item order is retained.
41: - Encrypted reasoning is opaque continuation data, not transcript text.
42: - Secrets never enter logs, fixtures, error messages, telemetry attributes, or request digests.
43: - Retry is allowed only before the first model content/tool emission from an attempt.
44: - Admission runs before every network request, including tool continuations and fallbacks.
45: - Cached input tokens still occupy the context window.
46: 
47: ## 4. Canonical Provider Input
48: 
49: The provider adapter receives a fully projected `CanonicalRequest`; it does not read session storage itself.
50: 
51: ```rust
52: struct CanonicalRequest {
53:     profile: ProviderProfileId,
54:     protocol: ProtocolId,
55:     model: String,
56:     instruction_blocks: Vec<InstructionBlock>,
57:     messages: Vec<ConversationMessage>,
58:     tools: Vec<ToolDefinition>,
59:     tool_choice: ToolChoice,
60:     reasoning: ReasoningRequest,
61:     max_output_tokens: Option<u32>,
62:     temperature: Option<f32>,
63:     continuation: Option<ProviderContinuation>,
64: }
65: ```
66: 
67: ### 4.1 Instruction blocks
68: 
69: Only these kinds exist in v1, and the request builder orders them exactly as listed:
70: 
71: 1. `SystemPolicy`
72: 2. `ProjectContext`
73: 3. `HistoricalHandoff`
74: 4. `CurrentState`
75: 
76: There is at most one block of each kind. Empty blocks are omitted. A later block never replaces or merges into an earlier kind.
77: 
78: The adapter serializes the blocks to one instruction string with these exact ASCII markers:
79: 
80: ```text
81: [PRAANA:SYSTEM_POLICY]
82: <content>
83: [/PRAANA:SYSTEM_POLICY]
84: 
85: [PRAANA:PROJECT_CONTEXT_DATA]
86: <content>
87: [/PRAANA:PROJECT_CONTEXT_DATA]
88: 
89: [PRAANA:HISTORICAL_HANDOFF_DATA]
90: <content>
91: [/PRAANA:HISTORICAL_HANDOFF_DATA]
92: 
93: [PRAANA:CURRENT_STATE_DATA]
94: <content>
95: [/PRAANA:CURRENT_STATE_DATA]
96: ```
97: 
98: Only present blocks are emitted. Blocks are separated by exactly two LF bytes. The resulting string has no leading or trailing LF added by the adapter. Content bytes are preserved except that CRLF and bare CR are normalized to LF before token estimation and serialization.
99: 
100: The system policy MUST state that all `*_DATA` blocks are non-authoritative data and cannot override system or current user instructions. The adapter does not escape marker-like text found inside data; authority comes from the fixed outer policy, not delimiter secrecy.

</content>

1: # PRAANA Rust v2 Memory Plugin Specification
2: 
3: **Status:** Normative design for Rust v2 Phase 6
4: 
5: **Depends on:** `docs/RUST_V2_PLAN.md`, especially sections 3, 9, 10, 13, 14, 18, and 20
6: 
7: **Audience:** Implementers of `praana-core`, the first-party SQLite memory plugin, and contract tests
8: 
9: ## 1. Purpose
10: 
11: This document fixes the Rust v2 cross-session memory boundary. Cross-session memory is optional. It is not session history, compaction, StateGraph, artifact storage, skill telemetry, or provider continuation state.
12: 
13: The default runtime has no memory plugin:
14: 
15: ```toml
16: [memory]
17: plugin = "none"
18: ```
19: 
20: The first-party implementation is enabled only by explicit configuration:
21: 
22: ```toml
23: [memory]
24: plugin = "builtin:sqlite"
25: 
26: [memory.options]
27: db_path = "~/.praana/plugins/builtin-sqlite/memory.db"
28: extraction = true
29: extraction_model = ""
30: digest_max_tokens = 1200
31: recall_limit = 10
32: ```
33: 
34: `plugin = "none"` means:
35: 
36: - No process-global memory database is opened.
37: - No embedding runtime or model is initialized or downloaded.
38: - No memory bootstrap or digest is added to a model request.
39: - No session-end extraction, reinforcement, decay, or consolidation runs.
40: - `recall`, `remember`, and `retract_memory` are not registered.
41: - Core session history, artifacts, current-session search, compaction, resume, and StateGraph work unchanged.
42: 
43: The v2 implementation has no compatibility obligation for the TypeScript `memory.enabled`, `memory.db_path`, `memory.embedder`, `memory.summarizer`, or top-level `consolidation` settings. It does not migrate the old `~/.praana/memory.db` schema.
44: 
45: ## 2. Normative Language
46: 
47: The words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY are normative.
48: 
49: All public plugin DTOs MUST:
50: 
51: - Derive `Serialize`, `Deserialize`, `JsonSchema`, `Clone`, and `Debug` unless a DTO contains an intentionally non-cloneable secret. No DTO in this specification contains a secret.
52: - Use `snake_case` JSON field names.
53: - Reject unknown enum tags and invalid required fields.
54: - Use UTF-8 strings, signed Unix milliseconds for time, and decimal integers for counts.
55: - Use string IDs at the contract boundary. The built-in plugin uses ULIDs, but consumers MUST treat IDs as opaque.
56: - Use tagged enums with `type` as the discriminator and `data` as the payload when a payload is required.
57: - Never serialize Rust type names, paths, backtraces, or `Debug` output as protocol data.
58: 
59: ## 3. Ownership and Invariants
60: 
61: ### 3.1 Core owns
62: 
63: - Canonical session events and their durable ordering.
64: - The accepted-conversation projection.
65: - Provider requests, credentials, and provider-native continuation data.
66: - Current-session artifact bodies and search indexes.
67: - StateGraph storage and projection.
68: - History compaction and historical handoffs.
69: - Tool registration and execution.
70: - Redaction before plugin-visible tool observations are constructed.
71: - Plugin call deadlines, cancellation, panic containment, telemetry, and disablement.
72: 
73: ### 3.2 A memory plugin owns
74: 
75: - Its storage backend, schema, migrations, and maintenance.
76: - Learning extraction and extraction prompt versions.
77: - Startup digest selection and rendering.
78: - Recall candidate generation, ranking, and filtering.
79: - Scope policy within the scope identifiers granted by core.
80: - Deduplication, contradiction handling, tombstones, pinning, and retraction.
81: - Validity, usefulness, reinforcement, decay, promotion, pruning, and consolidation.
82: - Session-end learning and artifact-summary promotion decisions.
83: - Any optional semantic index or embedding integration that it advertises.
84: 
85: ### 3.3 Hard invariants
86: 
87: - Core MUST compile and pass all non-memory tests with no memory implementation linked into the active session.
88: - No core module may import a built-in plugin database type, schema constant, or ranking helper.
89: - Core history compaction MUST NOT call a memory plugin and MUST NOT depend on a memory digest.
90: - A memory plugin failure MUST NOT prevent session creation, resume, a provider turn, a tool call, compaction, event durability, or shutdown.
91: - A plugin result is untrusted data. Core MUST bound it, validate it, label model-visible memory as non-authoritative historical evidence, and never promote it to system authority.
92: - Loading or disabling a memory plugin MUST NOT change canonical conversation projection semantics.
93:

95: 
96: Initial placement is deliberately in-process:

99: crates/praana-core/src/memory/
100:   mod.rs

1: # PRAANA Rust v2 Tool Runtime Specification
2: 
3: **Status:** Normative design for Rust v2 Phases 3, 4, 6, and 8
4: 
5: **Depends on:** `docs/RUST_V2_PLAN.md`, especially canonical events, artifacts, safety pipeline, and implementation phases
6: 
7: **Audience:** Implementers of `praana-core` tools, hooks, shell supervision, artifacts, provider adapters, and tests
8: 
9: ## 1. Purpose
10: 
11: This document fixes the Rust v2 tool runtime contract. It replaces the current loose TypeScript `defineTool({ description, parameters, execute })` registry with typed Rust tools, generated deterministic schemas, one ordered safety pipeline, durable execution events, bounded concurrency, and cross-platform process-tree supervision.
12: 
13: The runtime MUST preserve this logical order:
14: 
15: ```text
16: pre-tool:
17:   plan -> validate -> risk -> circuit -> write lock
18: 
19: execute
20: 
21: post-tool:
22:   LSP -> verify -> enrich -> redact -> circuit accounting -> write lock release
23: ```
24: 
25: No tool may bypass this pipeline by calling its implementation directly from a provider adapter, slash command, plugin, IPC handler, or test runner. Non-model commands that intentionally reuse a tool MUST call `ToolRuntime::execute_batch` with an explicit origin.
26: 
27: ## 2. Design Decisions
28: 
29: - Tool request and response types are Rust structs and enums.
30: - JSON Schema is generated from request types using Schemars, normalized, and snapshot-tested.
31: - Provider-visible tool order is explicit and independent of hash-map order, registration timing, capabilities, or filesystem discovery.
32: - Only core built-ins and core-owned standard memory adapters may register model-visible tools in v1.
33: - A tool describes capabilities and computes a call-specific `ToolIntent` before safety hooks run.
34: - Accepted provider tool calls in one assistant step form one batch. Admitted calls execute concurrently within limits.
35: - Preflight is deterministic in provider call order. Risk confirmations are serialized.
36: - Mutating paths use non-waiting per-path locks. A conflicting call receives a stable error rather than waiting behind an unknown side effect.
37: - Tool results are structured DTOs. The exact same finalized DTO feeds canonical events, artifacts/previews, provider tool-result messages, and UI events.
38: - Redaction is fail-closed before finalized results or artifacts become durable.
39: - Shell output is captured without blocking the Tokio reactor. Large output is artifactized; raw terminal streaming is disabled by default.
40: - Unix process groups and Windows Job Objects are mandatory, not optional platform enhancements.
41: 
42: ## 3. Module Layout
43: 
44: ```text
45: crates/praana-core/src/tools/
46:   mod.rs
47:   contract.rs          # typed and erased traits, DTOs
48:   registry.rs          # registration, ordering, schema catalog
49:   runtime.rs           # batch state machine
50:   result.rs            # canonical serialization and artifactization input
51:   error.rs             # stable codes
52:   intent.rs            # effects, paths, risk facts
53:   locks.rs              # normalized per-path lock table
54:   cancellation.rs      # session/turn/call cancellation hierarchy
55:   shell/
56:     mod.rs
57:     env.rs
58:     capture.rs
59:     unix.rs
60:     windows.rs
61:   builtin/
62:     files.rs
63:     edit.rs
64:     search.rs
65:     tests.rs
66:     git.rs
67:     state.rs
68:     artifacts.rs
69:     session_search.rs
70: 
71: crates/praana-core/src/hooks/
72:   mod.rs
73:   plan.rs
74:   validate.rs
75:   risk.rs
76:   circuit.rs
77:   lsp.rs
78:   verify.rs
79:   enrich.rs
80:   redact.rs
81: ```
82: 
83: The provider layer receives a read-only `ToolCatalog` and submits `ProviderToolCall` values to `ToolRuntime`. It does not own tool implementations.
84: 
85: ## 4. Identifiers and DTO Conventions
86: 
87: ```rust
88: pub struct ToolName(String);
89: pub struct ToolCallId(String);
90: pub struct ToolBatchId(String);
91: pub struct ToolExecutionId(String);
92: ```
93: 
94: Rules:
95: 
96: - Tool names match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$`.
97: - Provider call IDs are opaque UTF-8 strings, 1 to 256 bytes.
98: - A missing provider call ID is replaced at adapter ingress with a core ULID and the adapter records that synthesis.
99: - A batch ID and execution ID are core-generated ULIDs.
100: - Tool names and call IDs are never inferred from array position.

1: # PRAANA Rust v2 Temporary OpenTUI IPC Specification
2: 
3: **Status:** Normative design for Rust v2 Phase 7
4: 
5: **Lifetime:** Temporary migration protocol between the TypeScript OpenTUI client and the long-lived Rust process
6: 
7: **Depends on:** `docs/RUST_V2_PLAN.md`, `docs/RUST_V2_TOOL_RUNTIME_SPEC.md`, and the canonical event protocol
8: 
9: ## 1. Purpose
10: 
11: During migration, the existing TypeScript/OpenTUI application becomes a presentation client for the Rust core. It MUST NOT own session history, provider turns, tool execution, safety decisions, artifacts, StateGraph, compaction, memory lifecycle, model switching, credentials, or durable settings.
12: 
13: The TypeScript process spawns one long-lived Rust child and communicates over stdin/stdout using bounded one-line JSON frames. Rust stderr is reserved for diagnostics. This is not N-API, a shared library ABI, a network protocol, or a permanent public API.
14: 
15: ```text
16: TypeScript/OpenTUI process
17:   UI state, editor, overlays, transcript viewport
18:               |
19:               | child stdin/stdout: framed JSONL
20:               v
21: Long-lived Rust `praana core --ipc-stdio`
22:   sessions, turns, providers, tools, safety, history, artifacts, settings
23:               |
24:               +---- child stderr: logs only
25: ```
26: 
27: ## 2. Non-Goals
28: 
29: - Hosting the Rust turn engine through N-API.
30: - Supporting TCP, WebSocket, Unix socket, named pipe, or remote clients in Phase 7.
31: - Providing a stable third-party automation API.
32: - Sending raw artifact bodies or complete historical transcripts in unsolicited events.
33: - Preserving compatibility after the TypeScript client is deleted.
34: - Reusing this transport as the external memory plugin protocol without a separate security review.
35: 
36: ## 3. Process Contract
37: 
38: The TypeScript client spawns without a shell:
39: 
40: ```text
41: praana core --ipc-stdio --parent-pid <decimal-pid>
42: ```
43: 
44: Rules:
45: 
46: - Child stdin is protocol input.
47: - Child stdout is protocol output and MUST contain no banner, log, progress text, ANSI escape sequence, or blank line.
48: - Child stderr is UTF-8 diagnostics and MUST contain no protocol frames.
49: - The client reads stdout and stderr concurrently from process start.
50: - The client MUST NOT parse stderr as JSON protocol data, even if a line looks like JSON.
51: - The child exits when stdin reaches EOF, after cancelling active work and durably recording an interruption where possible.
52: - The child monitors the parent PID every two seconds. If the parent disappears and stdin has not closed, it performs the same shutdown.
53: - Normal shutdown is requested through `runtime.shutdown`; stdin EOF is the crash fallback.
54: - The client uses argument arrays, never shell interpolation, to spawn the binary.
55: 
56: One Rust process owns one active interactive session at a time in Phase 7. It may end that session and create/resume another without restarting.
57: 
58: ## 4. Framing
59: 
60: Each frame is exactly one JSON object encoded as UTF-8 followed by LF (`0x0a`). JSON strings escape embedded newlines. A sender MUST NOT pretty-print frames.
61: 
62: The receiver MAY accept CRLF by discarding one `0x0d` immediately before LF. All other unescaped ASCII control bytes are invalid.
63: 
64: Limits:
65: 
66: ```text
67: hard frame bytes excluding LF:       1,048,576
68: normal generated frame target:         262,144
69: maximum JSON nesting depth:                  64
70: maximum object members:                  4,096
71: maximum array elements:                 10,000
72: maximum individual JSON string bytes:   524,288
73: maximum in-flight requests:                  64
74: ```
75: 
76: Protocol parsers MUST:
77: 
78: - Decode UTF-8 strictly.
79: - Reject duplicate object keys.
80: - Reject non-integer JSON numbers where an integer is required.
81: - Reject NaN/infinity representations.
82: - Stop reading and terminate the connection on an over-limit unterminated frame.
83: - Return a structured error for a complete malformed frame when a valid request ID can be recovered; otherwise emit one stderr diagnostic and terminate.
84: 
85: Large transcript and artifact content is paged or referenced. Increasing the frame limit to carry a large payload is non-conforming.
86: 
87: ## 5. Versioning and Handshake
88: 
89: ### 5.1 Version policy
90: 
91: `v` is the protocol major version. Version `1` is defined here.
92: 
93: - A breaking envelope, command, event, or required-field change increments `v`.
94: - Additive commands/events/optional fields use capability negotiation and do not increment `v` during the temporary protocol lifetime.
95: - A receiver ignores unknown optional fields only after handshake.
96: - An unknown command or event name is never silently treated as another type.
97: - The server supports exactly one selected major per connection.
98: 
99: ### 5.2 First frame
100:

</content>

1: # PRAANA Rust v2 Ratatui Specification
2: 
3: **Status:** Normative design for Rust v2 Phase 9
4: 
5: **End state:** One standalone Rust executable with an in-process Ratatui UI and no Bun, TypeScript, OpenTUI, Solid, N-API, or `.node` sidecar
6: 
7: **Depends on:** `docs/RUST_V2_PLAN.md`, `docs/RUST_V2_TOOL_RUNTIME_SPEC.md`, and `docs/RUST_V2_IPC_SPEC.md`
8: 
9: ## 1. Purpose
10: 
11: This document fixes the final all-Rust terminal UI architecture, retained OpenTUI behavior, virtual transcript contract, dependency choices, state/update/render model, bounds, tests, performance thresholds, cutover plan, and TypeScript deletion gate.
12: 
13: Ratatui work starts only after the Rust headless core and temporary TypeScript IPC bridge are stable. The TUI is a client of core services inside the same process. It does not become a second owner of session, provider, tool, artifact, memory, or history state.
14: 
15: ## 2. Current Oracle and Required Correction
16: 
17: The behavioral oracle is the current TypeScript implementation under:
18: 
19: ```text
20: src/app-controller.ts
21: src/ui-events.ts
22: src/ui/tui/
23: src/ui/tui/prompt/
24: src/ui/tui/overlays/
25: src/ui/tui/transcript/
26: tests/*tui*
27: tests/*transcript*
28: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-virtual-transcript-design.md
29: ```
30: 
31: The current UI already has:
32: 
33: - A Solid/OpenTUI app shell, prompt, transcript, overlays, spinner, toasts, launch canvas, identity bar, and glance bar.
34: - Multiline editing, auto-grow, history, large-paste chips, path completion, and a slash palette.
35: - Model, login, logout, setup, consent, slash-result, and palette overlays.
36: - Streaming assistant/thinking rows, pending/finished tool rows, recall chips, system rows, and turn footers.
37: - Markdown and syntax-theme hooks.
38: - Keyboard transcript focus and tool/thinking expansion.
39: - A lightweight transcript index and lazy tool-result references.
40: 
41: The current implementation is not the final virtualization oracle by itself: `TranscriptStore.loadIndex` flattens every group and `TranscriptView` renders every entry. Rust MUST implement the approved virtual transcript design rather than porting this retained-all behavior. Valid historical content remains reachable while mounted rows and heavy bodies remain bounded.
42: 
43: ## 3. Locked Decisions
44: 
45: - Use Ratatui with the Crossterm backend.
46: - Use one reducer-owned `AppState`; widgets do not own authoritative mutable state.
47: - Core emits typed semantic `UiEvent` values through a sink. It never calls Ratatui and never writes terminal bytes.
48: - UI actions become typed `CoreCommand` values. Widgets never call session/tool/provider stores directly.
49: - The direct in-process command/event boundary uses Rust DTOs, not serialized JSONL. It preserves the same semantics as the temporary IPC protocol.
50: - Use an alternate screen and raw mode for the full TUI. Provide a plain line-mode fallback.
51: - Implement the prompt editor in PRAANA using `ropey`; do not use `tui-textarea`.
52: - Virtualize transcript by complete outer-turn groups and visual lines.
53: - Page heavy detail from core-owned history/artifacts. Do not retain full historical tool/thinking bodies in UI state.
54: - Preserve scroll anchors across prepend, append, eviction, expansion, collapse, resize, and reflow.
55: - Follow live output only when the viewport was already at the tail.
56: - No feature may require mouse input or color perception.
57: - Never render raw ANSI/OSC/control sequences from provider, user, tool, artifact, or log text.
58: 
59: ## 4. Dependencies
60: 
61: Use workspace-managed dependencies with these feature choices. Cargo.lock pins exact transitive versions for release builds.
62: 
63: ```toml
64: [dependencies]
65: ratatui = { version = "0.29", default-features = false, features = ["crossterm", "underline-color"] }
66: crossterm = { version = "0.28", features = ["event-stream"] }
67: tokio = { version = "1", features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread", "signal", "sync", "time"] }
68: tokio-util = { version = "0.7", features = ["rt"] }
69: futures = "0.3"
70: ropey = "1.6"
71: unicode-segmentation = "1.12"
72: unicode-width = "0.2"
73: textwrap = { version = "0.16", default-features = false, features = ["unicode-width"] }
74: pulldown-cmark = { version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["simd"] }
75: syntect = { version = "5.2", default-features = false, features = ["default-syntaxes", "default-themes", "parsing", "regex-fancy"] }
76: fuzzy-matcher = "0.3"
77: lru = "0.12"
78: 
79: [dev-dependencies]
80: insta = "1"
81: proptest = "1"
82: portable-pty = "0.9"
83: vt100 = "0.15"
84: criterion = "0.5"
85: ```
86: 
87: Rules:
88: 
89: - Do not add another terminal abstraction, async runtime, editor widget, Markdown renderer, or syntax engine.
90: - Do not enable Crossterm serde/event serialization in production.
91: - Do not enable Syntect Oniguruma. `regex-fancy` keeps the default binary free of that native dependency.
92: - `portable-pty`, `vt100`, Insta, and Criterion are test/dev dependencies only.
93: - Release binaries use rustls through the core provider stack; the TUI adds no TLS/network dependency.
94: - If the listed major/minor pair is unavailable or has a security advisory at implementation time, update this document in the same design-review change before substituting it. The implementer does not silently choose an alternative library.
95: 
96: ## 5. Crate and Module Layout
97: 
98: Ratatui belongs in `praana-cli`; reusable semantic UI DTOs and the event sink belong in `praana-core`.
